title.en: The Verb "To Be" — am / is / are
title.uz: "To be" feʼli — am / is / are
title.ru: Глагол «To Be» — am / is / are

rule.uz: Ingliz tilida 'boʻlmoq' feʼli shaxsga qarab am, is yoki are boʻladi va deyarli har doim gapda boʻlishi shart.
rule.ru: В английском глагол 'быть' меняется в зависимости от лица: am, is или are — и почти всегда обязательно присутствует в предложении.

en: In English, the verb "to be" changes depending on who you're talking about: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are. Unlike Uzbek, English almost never drops this verb — even in short sentences like "I am tired" or "The load is heavy," the am/is/are must be there.
In speech, English speakers usually shorten it: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're. Both forms are correct — contractions just sound more natural.
uz: Ingliz tilida "to be" feʼli kim haqida gapirayotganingizga qarab oʻzgaradi: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are. Oʻzbek tilidan farqli oʻlaroq, ingliz tili bu feʼlni deyarli hech qachon tushirib qoldirmaydi — hatto "I am tired" yoki "The load is heavy" kabi qisqa gaplarda ham am/is/are boʻlishi shart.
Ogʻzaki nutqda inglizlar buni odatda qisqartiradi: Iʼm, youʼre, heʼs, sheʼs, itʼs, weʼre, theyʼre. Ikkala shakl ham toʻgʻri — qisqartmalar shunchaki tabiiyroq eshitiladi.
ru: В английском глагол «to be» меняется в зависимости от того, о ком вы говорите: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are. В отличие от узбекского (и русского), английский почти никогда не опускает этот глагол — даже в коротких фразах вроде «I am tired» или «The load is heavy» слова am/is/are обязательны.
В речи англичане обычно сокращают его: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're. Обе формы правильны — сокращения просто звучат естественнее.

examples.en: I am a truck driver.
You are late today.
He is at the weigh station.
The trailer is heavy.
We are ready to go.

mistake.wrong: I driver. The load heavy.
mistake.right: I am a driver. The load is heavy.

why.en: Uzbek often leaves out 'bo'lmoq' in the present tense (u haydovchi — literally "he driver"), so it feels natural to drop am/is/are in English too. English needs it every time.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida hozirgi zamonda 'boʻlmoq' feʼli koʻpincha tushirib qoldiriladi (u haydovchi — soʻzma-soʻz "u haydovchi"), shuning uchun inglizchada ham am/is/are ni tushirib qoldirish tabiiy tuyuladi. Ingliz tilida u har safar kerak.
why.ru: В узбекском (как и в русском) в настоящем времени глагол 'быть' часто опускается (u haydovchi — буквально «он водитель»), поэтому кажется естественным пропускать am/is/are и в английском. В английском он нужен каждый раз.

q.en: The short form of 'she is' is:

teach: Drill out loud before explaining the rule: point at yourself (I am), the student (you are), a third object (it is) rapidly in random order until answers are automatic — Uzbek speakers often know the rule but still drop the verb under pressure.
Catch every dropped am/is/are in speaking practice immediately; it's the single most common Uzbek-speaker slip in this course.

title.en: Nouns, Articles & Plurals — a / an / the
title.uz: Otlar, artikllar va koʻplik — a / an / the
title.ru: Существительные, артикли и множественное число — a / an / the

rule.uz: Oʻzbek tilida artikl (a, an, the) yoʻq, shuning uchun bu ingliz tilidagi eng qiyin qoidalardan biri.
rule.ru: В узбекском (и русском) артиклей (a, an, the) нет, поэтому это одно из самых трудных правил английского.

en: Uzbek has no articles at all — this is genuinely one of the hardest parts of English for Uzbek speakers, so don't worry if it takes time. Use 'a' or 'an' the first time you mention something, when it could be any one of many: "I need a wrench" (any wrench). Use 'an' before a vowel sound: an inspector, an hour.
Use 'the' when both speakers already know which one you mean: "Park at the truck stop" (the specific one you both know), or when there's only one: "the highway we're on."
For general statements about a whole category (plural, no specific one), use no article at all: "Trucks need regular inspections" (trucks in general).
uz: Oʻzbek tilida artikllar umuman yoʻq — bu oʻzbekzabon oʻquvchilar uchun ingliz tilining haqiqatan eng qiyin qismlaridan biri, shuning uchun biroz vaqt ketsa, xavotir olmang. Biror narsani birinchi marta tilga olganingizda va u koʻplardan istalgan bittasi boʻlishi mumkin boʻlganda 'a' yoki 'an' ishlating: "I need a wrench" (istalgan kalit). Unli tovushdan oldin 'an' ishlating: an inspector, an hour.
Ikkala suhbatdosh qaysi biri haqida gapirayotganingizni bilganda 'the' ishlating: "Park at the truck stop" (ikkalangiz biladigan aniq bekat), yoki bitta boʻlganda: "the highway weʼre on."
Butun bir toifa haqidagi umumiy fikrlar uchun (koʻplik, aniq bittasi emas) umuman artikl ishlatilmaydi: "Trucks need regular inspections" (umuman yuk mashinalari).
ru: В узбекском артиклей нет вообще — и это действительно одна из самых сложных тем английского для узбекоговорящих, так что не переживайте, если на это уйдёт время. Используйте 'a' или 'an', когда упоминаете что-то впервые и это может быть любой из многих: «I need a wrench» (любой ключ). Используйте 'an' перед гласным звуком: an inspector, an hour.
Используйте 'the', когда оба собеседника уже знают, о чём речь: «Park at the truck stop» (та стоянка, которую вы оба знаете), или когда предмет один: «the highway we're on».
Для общих утверждений о целой категории (множественное число, ничего конкретного) артикль не нужен: «Trucks need regular inspections» (грузовики вообще).

examples.en: I need a wrench.
Call an inspector.
Park at the truck stop we always use.
examples.ru: Остановитесь на той стоянке, которой мы всегда пользуемся.

examples.en: Trucks need regular inspections.
The weigh station is open.

mistake.wrong: I saw inspector. Truck is on highway.
mistake.right: I saw an inspector. The truck is on the highway.

why.en: Since Uzbek has no equivalent word, it's easy to skip articles entirely. Native English speakers notice missing articles immediately, even though the sentence is still understandable.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida buning ekvivalenti boʻlmagani uchun artikllarni butunlay tushirib qoldirish oson. Ona tili ingliz boʻlganlar artikl yoʻqligini darhol sezadi, garchi gap baribir tushunarli boʻlsa ham.
why.ru: Поскольку в узбекском (и русском) нет соответствующего слова, артикли легко пропустить совсем. Носители английского сразу замечают их отсутствие, хотя предложение всё равно понятно.

q.en: 'Park at ___ truck stop we always use.' (a specific one)
q.uz: 'Park at ___ truck stop we always use.' (aniq bittasi)
q.ru: 'Park at ___ truck stop we always use.' (конкретная)

q.en: '___ trucks need regular inspections.' (trucks in general)
q.uz: '___ trucks need regular inspections.' (umuman yuk mashinalari)

q.en: 'She works at ___ warehouse downtown.' (one specific warehouse)
q.uz: 'She works at ___ warehouse downtown.' (bitta aniq ombor)
q.ru: 'She works at ___ warehouse downtown.' (один конкретный склад)

teach: Don't expect mastery — even advanced Uzbek speakers get articles wrong for years. Focus class time on the highest-value case: 'the' for something both people already know (the dispatcher, the load) vs 'a/an' for something new.
Quick drill: describe an object twice, first as brand new ('a wrench') then as already mentioned ('the wrench') — repetition builds the ear for it faster than the rule does.

title.uz: Hozirgi oddiy zamon — odatlar, faktlar va qoidalar
title.ru: Present Simple — привычки, факты и правила

rule.uz: Present Simple odatiy harakatlar, faktlar va qoidalar uchun ishlatiladi; he/she/it bilan feʼlga -s qoʻshiladi.
rule.ru: Present Simple используют для привычных действий, фактов и правил; с he/she/it к глаголу добавляется -s.

en: Use the present simple for routines, facts, and rules that are always true — not just what's happening this second. "I check my truck every morning" (a routine). "The speed limit changes here" (a fact). "Truckers file logs every day" (a rule).
The only tricky part: with he/she/it, add -s (or -es) to the verb: I check → he checks, I go → she goes, I do → it does.
uz: Present Simpleʼni odatlar, faktlar va doim toʻgʻri boʻlgan qoidalar uchun ishlating — faqat shu soniyada sodir boʻlayotgan narsa uchun emas. "I check my truck every morning" (odat). "The speed limit changes here" (fakt). "Truckers file logs every day" (qoida).
Yagona qiyin joyi: he/she/it bilan feʼlga -s (yoki -es) qoʻshiladi: I check → he checks, I go → she goes, I do → it does.
ru: Используйте Present Simple для привычек, фактов и правил, которые всегда верны — а не только для того, что происходит прямо сейчас. «I check my truck every morning» (привычка). «The speed limit changes here» (факт). «Truckers file logs every day» (правило).
Единственная сложность: с he/she/it к глаголу добавляется -s (или -es): I check → he checks, I go → she goes, I do → it does.

examples.en: I check my truck every morning.
examples.uz: Men har kuni ertalab mashinamni tekshiraman.
examples.ru: Каждое утро я проверяю свой грузовик.

examples.en: He drives for Speedline Logistics.
examples.ru: Он водит грузовик для Speedline Logistics.

examples.en: The speed limit changes here.
She works the night shift.
Drivers file their logs every day.

mistake.wrong: He drive fast. She check the oil.
mistake.right: He drives fast. She checks the oil.

why.en: Uzbek verb endings don't work like English -s. It's easy to forget the -s on he/she/it — but native speakers hear a missing -s immediately, the same way you'd hear a wrong word ending in Uzbek.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilidagi feʼl qoʻshimchalari inglizcha -s kabi ishlamaydi. he/she/it dagi -s ni unutish oson — lekin ona tili egalari -s yoʻqligini darhol eshitadi, xuddi siz oʻzbek tilida notoʻgʻri qoʻshimchani eshitgandek.
why.ru: Окончания глаголов в узбекском работают не так, как английское -s. Легко забыть -s у he/she/it, но носители языка сразу слышат его отсутствие — так же, как вы услышали бы неверное окончание в родном языке.

q.en: Which sentence describes a routine correctly?

teach: The -s ending is nearly silent in fast speech, so students often can't hear it even when it's said correctly — have them tap the table on '-s' sounds while reading examples aloud to build the habit by feel, not just by ear.

title.uz: Hozirgi davomli zamon — hozir sodir boʻlayotgan ish
title.ru: Present Continuous — прямо сейчас

rule.uz: am/is/are + feʼl-ing shakli hozir sodir boʻlayotgan yoki vaqtinchalik harakatni bildiradi.
rule.ru: am/is/are + глагол с -ing обозначают действие, которое происходит сейчас или временно.

en: Use am/is/are + verb-ing for something happening right now, or a temporary situation (not a permanent routine). "I am driving on I-40 right now." "We are waiting at the dock." "He is fixing the brakes."
Compare with present simple: "I drive a truck" (my job, a routine) vs. "I am driving to Dallas" (right now, this trip). Both are correct — they just answer different questions.
uz: Aynan hozir sodir boʻlayotgan yoki vaqtinchalik holat (doimiy odat emas) uchun am/is/are + feʼl-ing ishlating. "I am driving on I-40 right now." "We are waiting at the dock." "He is fixing the brakes."
Present Simple bilan solishtiring: "I drive a truck" (mening ishim, odat) va "I am driving to Dallas" (hozir, shu safar). Ikkalasi ham toʻgʻri — ular shunchaki turli savollarga javob beradi.
ru: Используйте am/is/are + глагол с -ing для того, что происходит прямо сейчас, или для временной ситуации (а не постоянной привычки). «I am driving on I-40 right now.» «We are waiting at the dock.» «He is fixing the brakes.»
Сравните с Present Simple: «I drive a truck» (моя работа, привычка) и «I am driving to Dallas» (сейчас, в этом рейсе). Оба варианта верны — они просто отвечают на разные вопросы.

examples.en: I am driving on I-40 right now.
We are waiting at the dock.
He is fixing the brakes.
The dispatcher is calling me.
They are loading the trailer now.

mistake.wrong: I drive to Dallas now. (for something happening this moment)
mistake.right: I am driving to Dallas now.

why.en: Because Uzbek's -yap- present tense often maps to English present simple in learners' minds, it's common to skip am/is/are + -ing for 'right now' actions. Use present simple only for routines and facts.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilidagi -yap- zamoni oʻquvchilar ongida koʻpincha inglizcha Present Simpleʼga toʻgʻri kelgani uchun, 'hozir' harakatlar uchun am/is/are + -ing ni tushirib qoldirish odatiy. Present Simpleʼni faqat odatlar va faktlar uchun ishlating.
why.ru: Поскольку узбекское время на -yap- часто соотносится в голове ученика с английским Present Simple, легко пропустить am/is/are + -ing для действий 'прямо сейчас'. Present Simple используйте только для привычек и фактов.

q.en: 'I ___ (drive) right now — call me back later.'
q.uz: 'I ___ (drive) right now — call me back later.'
q.ru: 'I ___ (drive) right now — call me back later.'

q.en: Which describes an action happening right now?
q.uz: Qaysi biri aynan hozir sodir boʻlayotgan harakatni tasvirlaydi?
q.ru: Какое предложение описывает действие, происходящее прямо сейчас?

opts: I check the engine every week.
I am checking the engine right now.

q.en: 'We usually ___ (eat) at this truck stop.' (routine, not now)
q.uz: 'We usually ___ (eat) at this truck stop.' (odat, hozir emas)
q.ru: 'We usually ___ (eat) at this truck stop.' (привычка, не сейчас)

teach: Contrast this directly against present-simple in the same lesson: 'I drive a truck' vs 'I am driving to Dallas' — side-by-side minimal pairs make the difference click faster than teaching either tense alone.

title.uz: Oʻtgan oddiy zamon — sodir boʻlgan voqeani aytib berish
title.ru: Past Simple — рассказ о том, что произошло

rule.uz: Muntazam feʼllarga -ed qoʻshiladi, lekin koʻp muhim feʼllar tartibsiz (notoʻgʻri) shaklga ega.
rule.ru: К правильным глаголам добавляется -ed, но многие важные глаголы неправильные — их формы нужно запоминать.

en: Use the past simple to report something that already happened — an inspection, an incident, a delivery. Regular verbs add -ed: check → checked, inspect → inspected, arrive → arrived.

Many common verbs are irregular and don't follow the -ed rule — these just have to be memorized: go → went, have → had, see → saw, drive → drove, hit → hit, break → broke, give → gave, find → found, tell → told.
uz: Allaqachon sodir boʻlgan narsani — tekshiruv, hodisa, yetkazib berishni — aytib berish uchun Past Simpleʼdan foydalaning. Muntazam feʼllarga -ed qoʻshiladi: check → checked, inspect → inspected, arrive → arrived.

Koʻplab keng tarqalgan feʼllar tartibsiz va -ed qoidasiga amal qilmaydi — ularni shunchaki yodlash kerak: go → went, have → had, see → saw, drive → drove, hit → hit, break → broke, give → gave, find → found, tell → told.
ru: Используйте Past Simple, чтобы рассказать о том, что уже произошло, — об осмотре, происшествии, доставке. Правильные глаголы принимают -ed: check → checked, inspect → inspected, arrive → arrived.

Многие частые глаголы неправильные и не следуют правилу -ed — их просто нужно выучить: go → went, have → had, see → saw, drive → drove, hit → hit, break → broke, give → gave, find → found, tell → told.

examples.en: I drove to Dallas yesterday.
The officer checked my logbook.
We arrived two hours late.
examples.uz: Biz ikki soat kech yetib keldik.
examples.ru: Мы прибыли на два часа позже.

examples.en: I saw an accident on the highway.
The trailer broke down near mile marker 90.

mistake.wrong: I drive to Dallas yesterday. I seen an accident.
mistake.right: I drove to Dallas yesterday. I saw an accident.

why.en: Two common slips: using the base verb instead of the past form after a past time word like 'yesterday,' and mixing up the past simple (saw) with the past participle (seen), which needs 'have' — 'I have seen,' not 'I seen.'
why.uz: Ikkita keng tarqalgan xato: 'yesterday' kabi oʻtgan zamon soʻzidan keyin oʻtgan shakl oʻrniga asosiy feʼlni ishlatish va Past Simple (saw) bilan 'have' talab qiluvchi oʻtgan zamon sifatdoshini (seen) chalkashtirish — 'I have seen', 'I seen' emas.
why.ru: Две частые ошибки: использование начальной формы глагола вместо прошедшей после слов вроде 'yesterday' и путаница между Past Simple (saw) и причастием прошедшего времени (seen), которому нужен 'have' — 'I have seen', а не 'I seen'.

q.en: Which sentence correctly reports a past event?
q.uz: Qaysi gap oʻtgan voqeani toʻgʻri aytib beradi?
q.ru: Какое предложение правильно рассказывает о прошлом событии?

teach: Irregular past-tense verbs (went, found, drove, said) are the real obstacle, not the grammar rule itself — spend most of class time drilling the irregular verbs that come up in this course rather than the regular -ed pattern, which students usually pick up quickly.

title.en: Talking About the Future — will / going to
title.uz: Kelasi zamon haqida gapirish — will / going to
title.ru: Разговор о будущем — will / going to

rule.uz: 'Will' qaror va vaʼdalar uchun, 'going to' esa oldindan rejalashtirilgan ishlar uchun ishlatiladi.
rule.ru: 'Will' используют для решений и обещаний, а 'going to' — для заранее запланированного.

en: Use 'will' for decisions made right now, promises, and predictions: "I will call dispatch" (deciding now), "I will be there by 6" (a promise). Will + base verb, no -ing.
Use 'going to' for plans you already made before this moment: "I'm going to deliver this afternoon" (already planned). Structure: am/is/are + going to + base verb.
In everyday speech the difference is small, but 'going to' sounds more like a fixed plan, while 'will' sounds more like a decision or offer in the moment.
uz: Hozir qabul qilingan qarorlar, vaʼdalar va bashoratlar uchun 'will' ishlating: "I will call dispatch" (hozir qaror qilaman), "I will be there by 6" (vaʼda). Will + asosiy feʼl, -ing siz.
Shu lahzadan oldin tuzilgan rejalar uchun 'going to' ishlating: "Iʼm going to deliver this afternoon" (oldindan rejalashtirilgan). Tuzilishi: am/is/are + going to + asosiy feʼl.
Kundalik nutqda farq kichik, lekin 'going to' qatʼiyroq reja kabi, 'will' esa oʻsha lahzadagi qaror yoki taklif kabi eshitiladi.
ru: Используйте 'will' для решений, принятых прямо сейчас, обещаний и предсказаний: «I will call dispatch» (решаю сейчас), «I will be there by 6» (обещание). Will + начальная форма глагола, без -ing.
Используйте 'going to' для планов, которые вы составили до этого момента: «I'm going to deliver this afternoon» (уже запланировано). Структура: am/is/are + going to + начальная форма глагола.
В повседневной речи разница небольшая, но 'going to' звучит как устойчивый план, а 'will' — скорее как решение или предложение в моменте.

examples.en: I will call dispatch now.
I'm going to deliver this afternoon.
It will rain later today.
We are going to stop at the next rest area.
examples.ru: Мы остановимся на следующей зоне отдыха (план).

examples.en: I'll text you my ETA.
examples.uz: Sizga taxminiy yetib borish vaqtimni SMS qilaman.
examples.ru: Я напишу вам своё расчётное время прибытия.

mistake.wrong: I go to Dallas tomorrow. (as a plan)
mistake.right: I'm going to go to Dallas tomorrow. / I will go to Dallas tomorrow.

why.en: Present simple alone doesn't mark future in English the way context sometimes does in Uzbek — you need 'will' or 'going to' to clearly mark future plans and decisions.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida kontekst baʼzan kelasi zamonni koʻrsatganidek, ingliz tilida faqat Present Simple buni koʻrsatmaydi — kelajakdagi reja va qarorlarni aniq koʻrsatish uchun 'will' yoki 'going to' kerak.
why.ru: Одного только Present Simple недостаточно, чтобы обозначить будущее так, как это иногда делает контекст в узбекском (и русском) — нужны 'will' или 'going to', чтобы ясно показать планы и решения на будущее.

q.en: Deciding right now: 'Okay, I ___ call dispatch.'
q.uz: Aynan hozir qaror qilish: 'Okay, I ___ call dispatch.'
q.ru: Решаете прямо сейчас: 'Okay, I ___ call dispatch.'

q.en: Already planned: 'I ___ deliver this load at 3 PM.' (planned yesterday)
q.uz: Oldindan rejalashtirilgan: 'I ___ deliver this load at 3 PM.' (kecha rejalashtirilgan)
q.ru: Уже запланировано: 'I ___ deliver this load at 3 PM.' (запланировано вчера)

q.en: 'It ___ rain later — look at those clouds.' (prediction)
q.uz: 'It ___ rain later — look at those clouds.' (bashorat)
q.ru: 'It ___ rain later — look at those clouds.' (предсказание)

q.en: Which is a promise made right now?
q.ru: Какое из этого — обещание, данное прямо сейчас?

q.en: 'We ___ stop at the next rest area.' (decided in advance)
q.uz: 'We ___ stop at the next rest area.' (oldindan qaror qilingan)
q.ru: 'We ___ stop at the next rest area.' (решено заранее)

q.en: The short form of 'I will' is:

teach: Keep it simple at this level: 'going to' for a plan already decided, 'will' for a decision made right now or a promise. Most real trucking talk only needs these two uses — don't over-explain finer native-speaker distinctions.

title.uz: Ha/Yoʻq savollari — Do / Does / Did
title.ru: Вопросы «да/нет» — Do / Does / Did

rule.uz: Ingliz tilida savol berish uchun gap boshiga Do, Does yoki Did qoʻyiladi — bu oʻzbek tilida yoʻq qoida.
rule.ru: В английском, чтобы задать вопрос, в начало предложения ставят Do, Does или Did — такого правила нет ни в узбекском, ни в русском.

en: This is one of the biggest structural differences between Uzbek and English. Uzbek turns a statement into a question with a small suffix (-mi) added to the word being asked about — no extra word is needed. English instead adds 'Do' (or 'Does' for he/she/it, 'Did' for past) to the FRONT of the sentence, and the main verb goes back to its base form.

Statement: "You have your CDL." → Question: "Do you have your CDL?" Statement: "She checked the oil." → Question: "Did she check the oil?" (checked → check, because 'did' already carries the past tense).
For 'to be,' there's no do/does/did — just move am/is/are to the front: "You are ready" → "Are you ready?"
uz: Bu oʻzbek va ingliz tillari orasidagi eng katta tuzilish farqlaridan biri. Oʻzbek tilida gap savolga soʻralayotgan soʻzga qoʻshiladigan kichik qoʻshimcha (-mi) bilan aylanadi — qoʻshimcha soʻz kerak emas. Ingliz tilida esa gapning OLDIGA 'Do' (he/she/it uchun 'Does', oʻtgan zamon uchun 'Did') qoʻyiladi va asosiy feʼl asl shakliga qaytadi.

Darak gap: "You have your CDL." → Savol: "Do you have your CDL?" Darak gap: "She checked the oil." → Savol: "Did she check the oil?" (checked → check, chunki 'did' oʻtgan zamonni allaqachon ifodalaydi).
'to be' uchun do/does/did kerak emas — shunchaki am/is/are ni oldinga oʻtkazing: "You are ready" → "Are you ready?"
ru: Это одно из самых больших структурных различий между узбекским и английским. В узбекском утверждение превращается в вопрос с помощью небольшого суффикса (-mi) у слова, о котором спрашивают, — дополнительное слово не нужно. В английском же в НАЧАЛО предложения добавляется 'Do' (или 'Does' для he/she/it, 'Did' для прошедшего), а основной глагол возвращается в начальную форму.

Утверждение: «You have your CDL.» → Вопрос: «Do you have your CDL?» Утверждение: «She checked the oil.» → Вопрос: «Did she check the oil?» (checked → check, потому что 'did' уже несёт прошедшее время).
С глаголом «to be» do/does/did не нужны — просто переставьте am/is/are в начало: «You are ready» → «Are you ready?»

examples.en: Do you have your CDL?
Does the load need a permit?
Did you inspect the brakes?
Are you ready to go?
Does this truck have a sleeper berth?
examples.ru: У этого грузовика есть спальное место?

mistake.wrong: You have your CDL? She checked the oil?
mistake.right: Do you have your CDL? Did she check the oil?

why.en: Without do/does/did, the sentence sounds like a surprised statement, not a real question, to a native English speaker — even though the meaning is guessable from tone alone.
why.uz: Do/does/did siz gap ona tili ingliz boʻlgan kishiga haqiqiy savol emas, balki hayron boʻlib aytilgan darak gap kabi eshitiladi — maʼnosi ohangdan taxmin qilinsa ham.
why.ru: Без do/does/did предложение звучит для носителя английского как удивлённое утверждение, а не настоящий вопрос — хотя смысл можно угадать по интонации.

q.en: '___ the load need a permit?' (load = it)
q.uz: '___ the load need a permit?' (load = it)
q.ru: '___ the load need a permit?' (load = it)

q.en: Turn into a question: 'She checked the oil.'
q.ru: Превратите в вопрос: 'She checked the oil.'

q.en: '___ you ready to go?' (using 'to be', no do/does)
q.uz: '___ you ready to go?' ('to be' bilan, do/does siz)
q.ru: '___ you ready to go?' (с 'to be', без do/does)

q.en: '___ this truck have a sleeper berth?'
q.uz: '___ this truck have a sleeper berth?'
q.ru: '___ this truck have a sleeper berth?'

teach: The word-order flip (Do you...? not You do...?) is the hard part, not vocabulary — drill the question pattern as a chant (Do + subject + verb) before moving to real content.

title.en: Wh- Questions — What / Where / When / Why / How
title.uz: Wh- savollari — What / Where / When / Why / How
title.ru: Вопросы с Wh- — What / Where / When / Why / How

rule.uz: Wh- soʻzi doim gap boshida keladi: Wh-soʻz + do/does/did (yoki is/are) + ega + feʼl.
rule.ru: Вопросительное слово всегда стоит в начале: Wh-слово + do/does/did (или is/are) + подлежащее + глагол.

en: Wh- questions (what, where, when, why, how, who) always start with the question word, followed by the same do/does/did (or is/are) pattern as yes/no questions: Wh-word + do/does/did + subject + verb.
"Where are you headed?" "What are you hauling?" "How long have you been driving?" "Why did you stop here?"

Uzbek word order is subject-object-verb, and the question word often stays near where the answer would go, not always at the front. In English, the question word must move all the way to the front of the sentence — always.
uz: Wh- savollar (what, where, when, why, how, who) doim soʻroq soʻz bilan boshlanadi, undan keyin ha/yoʻq savollaridagi kabi do/does/did (yoki is/are) tuzilishi keladi: Wh-soʻz + do/does/did + ega + feʼl.
"Where are you headed?" "What are you hauling?" "How long have you been driving?" "Why did you stop here?"

Oʻzbek tilida soʻz tartibi ega-toʻldiruvchi-feʼl boʻlib, soʻroq soʻz koʻpincha javob turadigan joyga yaqin turadi, doim ham boshda emas. Ingliz tilida soʻroq soʻz har doim gapning eng boshiga oʻtishi shart.
ru: Вопросы с Wh- (what, where, when, why, how, who) всегда начинаются с вопросительного слова, а дальше идёт та же схема с do/does/did (или is/are), что и в вопросах «да/нет»: Wh-слово + do/does/did + подлежащее + глагол.
«Where are you headed?» «What are you hauling?» «How long have you been driving?» «Why did you stop here?»

В узбекском порядок слов — подлежащее-дополнение-глагол, и вопросительное слово часто остаётся ближе к тому месту, где будет ответ, а не всегда в начале. В английском вопросительное слово всегда должно переместиться в самое начало предложения.

examples.en: Where are you headed?
What are you hauling?
How long have you been driving?
Why did you stop here?
When does the dock open?

mistake.wrong: You are headed where? You stopped here why?
mistake.right: Where are you headed? Why did you stop here?

why.en: In Uzbek, word order is more flexible, so the question word can feel natural at the end. In English, the Wh-word must move to the very front, every time.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida soʻz tartibi moslashuvchanroq, shuning uchun soʻroq soʻz oxirida turishi tabiiy tuyulishi mumkin. Ingliz tilida Wh-soʻz har safar eng boshiga oʻtishi kerak.
why.ru: В узбекском порядок слов более свободный, поэтому вопросительное слово в конце кажется естественным. В английском Wh-слово должно стоять в самом начале — каждый раз.

q.en: '___ is the dispatcher on the phone?' (asking a person)
q.uz: '___ is the dispatcher on the phone?' (odam haqida soʻrayapmiz)
q.ru: '___ is the dispatcher on the phone?' (спрашиваем о человеке)

teach: Teach wh-word + do/does/did + subject + verb as one fixed template ('Where do you...', 'What did you...') rather than explaining each wh-word separately — the structure is identical across all of them.

title.uz: Boʻlishsizlik — donʼt / doesnʼt / didnʼt / isnʼt
title.ru: Отрицания — don't / doesn't / didn't / isn't

rule.uz: 'To be' bilan 'not' qoʻshiladi (isnʼt, arenʼt); boshqa feʼllar bilan donʼt/doesnʼt/didnʼt ishlatiladi.
rule.ru: С 'to be' добавляют 'not' (isn't, aren't); с остальными глаголами используют don't/doesn't/didn't.

en: To make a sentence negative with 'to be,' just add 'not': is not (isn't), are not (aren't), was not (wasn't). "I am not tired" → "I'm not tired."
For every other verb, use don't/doesn't (present) or didn't (past) + the base verb — never add 'not' directly to the main verb. "I don't know." "He doesn't drive at night." "We didn't stop."
uz: 'to be' bilan gapni boʻlishsiz qilish uchun shunchaki 'not' qoʻshing: is not (isnʼt), are not (arenʼt), was not (wasnʼt). "I am not tired" → "Iʼm not tired."

Boshqa barcha feʼllar bilan donʼt/doesnʼt (hozirgi) yoki didnʼt (oʻtgan) + asosiy feʼldan foydalaning — hech qachon 'not' ni asosiy feʼlga toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri qoʻshmang. "I donʼt know." "He doesnʼt drive at night." "We didnʼt stop."
ru: Чтобы сделать предложение отрицательным с глаголом 'to be', просто добавьте 'not': is not (isn't), are not (aren't), was not (wasn't). «I am not tired» → «I'm not tired.»

Со всеми остальными глаголами используйте don't/doesn't (настоящее) или didn't (прошедшее) + начальную форму глагола — никогда не добавляйте 'not' прямо к основному глаголу. «I don't know.» «He doesn't drive at night.» «We didn't stop.»

examples.en: I don't know the address.
He doesn't drive at night.
We didn't stop at that station.
examples.ru: Мы не останавливались на той станции.

examples.en: The load isn't secure yet.
They aren't ready.

mistake.wrong: I not know. I no have time.
mistake.right: I don't know. I don't have time.

why.en: Uzbek negation attaches directly to the verb as a suffix (bil-ma-yman), so it's natural to try putting 'not' or 'no' directly next to the English verb. English instead needs don't/doesn't/didn't in front of the base verb.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida boʻlishsizlik feʼlga qoʻshimcha sifatida toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri qoʻshiladi (bil-ma-yman), shuning uchun inglizcha feʼlning yoniga 'not' yoki 'no' qoʻyishga urinish tabiiy. Ingliz tilida esa asosiy feʼl oldida donʼt/doesnʼt/didnʼt kerak.
why.ru: В узбекском отрицание присоединяется к глаголу как суффикс (bil-ma-yman), поэтому естественно пытаться поставить 'not' или 'no' прямо рядом с английским глаголом. В английском же перед начальной формой глагола нужны don't/doesn't/didn't.

teach: Students who've mastered yes/no questions usually pick up negatives fast, since both use do/does/did — teach this unit right after questions and point out the shared structure explicitly.

title.en: Must / Have To / Should — Rules & Advice
title.uz: Must / have to / should — qoida va maslahat
title.ru: Must / Have To / Should — правила и советы

rule.uz: 'Must' va 'have to' majburiyatni, 'should' esa maslahatni bildiradi; 'must not' va 'donʼt have to' esa qarama-qarshi maʼnoga ega.
rule.ru: 'Must' и 'have to' выражают обязанность, 'should' — совет; а 'must not' и 'don't have to' имеют противоположные значения.

en: Use 'must' or 'have to' for a rule or legal requirement: "You must stop at a weigh station" — both mean it's required. Use 'should' for advice, not a hard rule: "You should take a break" (a good idea, not the law).

WARNING — these two look similar but mean the OPPOSITE thing: "You must not park here" means it's forbidden (illegal). "You don't have to park here" means it's optional — you can if you want, but nobody's making you. Confusing these two completely reverses the meaning.
uz: Qoida yoki qonuniy talab uchun 'must' yoki 'have to' ishlating: "You must stop at a weigh station" — ikkalasi ham bu majburiy ekanini anglatadi. Maslahat uchun, qattiq qoida emas, 'should' ishlating: "You should take a break" (yaxshi fikr, qonun emas).

OGOHLANTIRISH — bu ikkalasi oʻxshash koʻrinadi, lekin QARAMA-QARSHI maʼnoni bildiradi: "You must not park here" bu taqiqlangan (noqonuniy) degani. "You donʼt have to park here" bu ixtiyoriy degani — xohlasangiz qilishingiz mumkin, lekin sizni hech kim majburlamaydi. Ularni chalkashtirish maʼnoni butunlay teskari qilib qoʻyadi.
ru: Используйте 'must' или 'have to' для правила или законного требования: «You must stop at a weigh station» — оба означают, что это обязательно. Используйте 'should' для совета, а не жёсткого правила: «You should take a break» (хорошая идея, но не закон).

ВНИМАНИЕ — эти две конструкции похожи, но значат ПРОТИВОПОЛОЖНОЕ: «You must not park here» означает, что это запрещено (незаконно). «You don't have to park here» означает, что это необязательно — можете, если хотите, но вас никто не заставляет. Если их перепутать, смысл полностью меняется.

examples.en: You must stop at every weigh station.
examples.uz: Har bir tarozi bekatida toʻxtashingiz shart.
examples.ru: Вы обязаны останавливаться на каждой весовой станции.

examples.en: Drivers have to carry a medical card.
examples.uz: Haydovchilar tibbiy karta olib yurishi kerak.
examples.ru: Водители обязаны возить с собой медицинскую карту.

examples.en: You should take a break every few hours.
examples.uz: Bir necha soatda tanaffus qilganingiz maʼqul.
examples.ru: Вам стоит делать перерыв каждые несколько часов.

examples.en: You must not park in a no-parking zone.
examples.ru: Нельзя парковаться в зоне, где парковка запрещена (запрещено).

examples.en: You don't have to fill out this form today.
examples.uz: Bu formani bugun toʻldirishingiz shart emas (ixtiyoriy).
examples.ru: Вам необязательно заполнять эту анкету сегодня (по желанию).

mistake.wrong: Treating 'must not' and 'don't have to' as the same thing.
mistake.right: Must not = forbidden. Don't have to = optional, not required.

why.en: These two are a common trap for English learners everywhere, not just Uzbek speakers — the negative forms of 'must' and 'have to' go in completely different directions, unlike the positive forms which mean almost the same thing.
why.uz: Bu ikkalasi nafaqat oʻzbekzabonlar, balki butun dunyodagi ingliz tili oʻrganuvchilar uchun keng tarqalgan tuzoq — 'must' va 'have to' ning boʻlishsiz shakllari butunlay boshqa tomonga ketadi, boʻlishli shakllari esa deyarli bir xil maʼnoni bildiradi.
why.ru: Эти две конструкции — частая ловушка для изучающих английский по всему миру, а не только для узбекоговорящих: отрицательные формы 'must' и 'have to' идут в совершенно разные стороны, тогда как утвердительные значат почти одно и то же.

q.en: 'You ___ stop at every weigh station.' (it's the law)
q.uz: 'You ___ stop at every weigh station.' (bu qonun)
q.ru: 'You ___ stop at every weigh station.' (это закон)

q.en: 'You ___ fill out this form.' (optional, not required)
q.uz: 'You ___ fill out this form.' (ixtiyoriy, majburiy emas)
q.ru: 'You ___ fill out this form.' (по желанию, необязательно)

q.en: 'You ___ take a break — you look tired.' (advice, not a rule)
q.uz: 'You ___ take a break — you look tired.' (maslahat, qoida emas)
q.ru: 'You ___ take a break — you look tired.' (совет, а не правило)

opts: You have to have a CDL.

q.en: 'Drivers ___ carry proof of insurance.' (required by law)
q.uz: 'Drivers ___ carry proof of insurance.' (qonun boʻyicha talab qilinadi)
q.ru: 'Drivers ___ carry proof of insurance.' (требуется по закону)

teach: 'Must' and 'have to' feel interchangeable to a beginner, but the real classroom value is teaching when NOT to use them — e.g. giving advice ('you should') vs stating a hard rule ('you must') matters a lot in DOT contexts.

title.uz: Can / could / may — qobiliyat va ruxsat
title.ru: Can / Could / May — умение и разрешение

rule.uz: 'Can' hozirgi qobiliyat/ruxsat, 'could' oʻtgan qobiliyat yoki xushmuomala soʻrov, 'may' rasmiy ruxsat uchun.
rule.ru: 'Can' — умение или разрешение в настоящем, 'could' — умение в прошлом или вежливая просьба, 'may' — официальное разрешение.

en: Use 'can' for present ability or informal permission: "I can drive a manual transmission" (ability), "Can I use the restroom?" (asking permission, casual). Use 'could' for past ability or a more polite request: "I could drive a manual truck when I was 20" (past ability), "Could you repeat that?" (polite).
Use 'may' for formal permission, often from an authority: "You may proceed" (an officer allowing you through). All three are followed by the base verb — never add -ing or -s.
uz: Hozirgi qobiliyat yoki norasmiy ruxsat uchun 'can' ishlating: "I can drive a manual transmission" (qobiliyat), "Can I use the restroom?" (ruxsat soʻrash, norasmiy). Oʻtgan qobiliyat yoki yanada muloyim soʻrov uchun 'could' ishlating: "I could drive a manual truck when I was 20" (oʻtgan qobiliyat), "Could you repeat that?" (muloyim).

Rasmiy ruxsat uchun, koʻpincha hokimiyat vakilidan, 'may' ishlating: "You may proceed" (ofitser sizni oʻtkazib yubormoqda). Uchalasidan keyin ham asosiy feʼl keladi — hech qachon -ing yoki -s qoʻshmang.
ru: Используйте 'can' для умения в настоящем или неформального разрешения: «I can drive a manual transmission» (умение), «Can I use the restroom?» (просьба о разрешении, неформально). Используйте 'could' для умения в прошлом или для более вежливой просьбы: «I could drive a manual truck when I was 20» (умение в прошлом), «Could you repeat that?» (вежливо).

Используйте 'may' для официального разрешения, часто от представителя власти: «You may proceed» (офицер пропускает вас). После всех трёх идёт начальная форма глагола — никогда не добавляйте -ing или -s.

examples.en: I can drive a manual transmission.
examples.uz: Men mexanika uzatmali mashinani hayday olaman.
examples.ru: Я умею водить механическую коробку передач.

examples.en: Can I see your license, please?
Could you repeat that?
You may proceed, sir.
I couldn't find the address last night.
examples.ru: Прошлой ночью я не смог найти адрес.

mistake.wrong: I can to drive. She can drives.
mistake.right: I can drive. She can drive.

why.en: After can/could/may, always use the base verb with no 'to' and no -s — even for he/she/it. This is different from most other verbs, so it's an easy slip.
why.uz: can/could/may dan keyin doim 'to' siz va -s siz asosiy feʼlni ishlating — he/she/it uchun ham. Bu koʻpchilik boshqa feʼllardan farq qiladi, shuning uchun adashish oson.
why.ru: После can/could/may всегда используйте начальную форму глагола без 'to' и без -s — даже с he/she/it. Это отличается от большинства других глаголов, поэтому легко ошибиться.

q.en: Most formal way to give permission:

teach: Can/could/may cover three different jobs (ability, past ability, permission) in one short word — ask three quick real-life questions in a row ('Can you drive stick?' 'Could you drive at 18?' 'May I park here?') so students feel the difference rather than memorize a list.

title.en: Prepositions of Place & Direction — at / in / on / to / from
title.uz: Oʻrin va yoʻnalish predloglari — at / in / on / to / from
title.ru: Предлоги места и направления — at / in / on / to / from

rule.uz: Oʻzbek tilida predloglar soʻzdan keyin qoʻshimcha sifatida keladi (uy-da), ingliz tilida esa alohida soʻz sifatida oldin keladi.
rule.ru: В узбекском предлоги стоят после слова как суффикс (uy-da), а в английском — отдельным словом перед ним.

en: Use 'at' for a specific point: at the weigh station, at mile marker 90. Use 'in' for something enclosed: in the cab, in the trailer, in Texas. Use 'on' for a surface or route: on the highway, on I-40, on the dock.

For direction, use 'to' (destination) and 'from' (origin): "I'm driving to Dallas from Houston." Use 'onto' when getting onto a surface (merge onto the highway) and 'into' when entering an enclosed space (walk into the office).

Uzbek attaches this meaning as a suffix directly onto the noun (uy-da = "at home"), while English uses a separate word placed BEFORE the noun. Getting the position right, and picking the right one of at/in/on, both take practice.
uz: Aniq nuqta uchun 'at' ishlating: at the weigh station, at mile marker 90. Yopiq narsa uchun 'in' ishlating: in the cab, in the trailer, in Texas. Sirt yoki yoʻnalish uchun 'on' ishlating: on the highway, on I-40, on the dock.

Yoʻnalish uchun 'to' (borish joyi) va 'from' (chiqish joyi) ishlating: "Iʼm driving to Dallas from Houston." Sirtga chiqayotganda 'onto' (merge onto the highway), yopiq joyga kirayotganda 'into' (walk into the office) ishlating.

Oʻzbek tilida bu maʼno qoʻshimcha sifatida toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri otga qoʻshiladi (uy-da = "at home"), ingliz tilida esa otdan OLDIN alohida soʻz ishlatiladi. Toʻgʻri oʻrinni topish ham, at/in/on dan toʻgʻrisini tanlash ham mashq talab qiladi.
ru: Используйте 'at' для конкретной точки: at the weigh station, at mile marker 90. Используйте 'in' для чего-то замкнутого: in the cab, in the trailer, in Texas. Используйте 'on' для поверхности или маршрута: on the highway, on I-40, on the dock.

Для направления используйте 'to' (пункт назначения) и 'from' (откуда): «I'm driving to Dallas from Houston.» Используйте 'onto', когда выезжаете на поверхность (merge onto the highway), и 'into', когда входите в замкнутое пространство (walk into the office).

В узбекском это значение присоединяется суффиксом прямо к существительному (uy-da = «дома»), а в английском используется отдельное слово, стоящее ПЕРЕД существительным. И правильное положение слова, и выбор между at/in/on требуют практики.

examples.en: Meet me at the truck stop.
examples.uz: Meni yuk mashinalari bekatida kutib turing.

examples.en: The documents are in the glove box.
We're on Interstate 40 now.
I'm driving to Dallas from Houston.
examples.ru: Я еду в Даллас из Хьюстона.

examples.en: Merge onto the highway carefully.

mistake.wrong: I am truck stop. Documents glove box.
mistake.right: I am at the truck stop. The documents are in the glove box.

why.en: Because Uzbek marks location with a suffix on the noun itself, it's easy to forget that English needs a separate preposition word before the noun — dropping it entirely, not just picking the wrong one, is the most common version of this mistake.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida joylashuv otning oʻziga qoʻshimcha bilan belgilangani uchun, ingliz tilida otdan oldin alohida predlog soʻzi kerakligini unutish oson — bu xatoning eng keng tarqalgan koʻrinishi notoʻgʻri predlogni tanlash emas, uni butunlay tushirib qoldirishdir.
why.ru: Поскольку в узбекском местоположение обозначается суффиксом на самом существительном, легко забыть, что в английском нужен отдельный предлог перед существительным — самая частая ошибка здесь не выбор неверного предлога, а его полное отсутствие.

q.en: 'The documents are ___ the glove box.' (enclosed space)
q.uz: 'The documents are ___ the glove box.' (yopiq joy)
q.ru: 'The documents are ___ the glove box.' (замкнутое пространство)

teach: Prepositions rarely translate word-for-word from Uzbek, so treat 'at the dock', 'in the cab', 'on the highway' as fixed phrases to memorize rather than deriving them from a rule — flashcards work better here than explanation.

title.en: Prepositions of Time — at / in / on / for / since
title.uz: Vaqt predloglari — at / in / on / for / since
title.ru: Предлоги времени — at / in / on / for / since

rule.uz: at — aniq vaqt, in — oy/yil/davr, on — kun/sana, for — davomiylik, since — boshlanish nuqtasi.
rule.ru: at — точное время, in — месяц/год/период, on — день/дата, for — длительность, since — точка начала.

en: Use 'at' for a clock time: at 6 AM, at noon, at midnight. Use 'in' for a month, year, or longer period: in July, in 2024, in the morning. Use 'on' for a specific day or date: on Monday, on July 4th.

Use 'for' to say how long something lasts: for three hours, for two weeks. Use 'since' to say when something started: since morning, since Monday — since always pairs with a starting point, not a length of time.
uz: Soat vaqti uchun 'at' ishlating: at 6 AM, at noon, at midnight. Oy, yil yoki uzoqroq davr uchun 'in' ishlating: in July, in 2024, in the morning. Aniq kun yoki sana uchun 'on' ishlating: on Monday, on July 4th.

Biror narsa qancha davom etishini aytish uchun 'for' ishlating: for three hours, for two weeks. Biror narsa qachon boshlanganini aytish uchun 'since' ishlating: since morning, since Monday — 'since' doim boshlanish nuqtasi bilan keladi, vaqt uzunligi bilan emas.
ru: Используйте 'at' для времени по часам: at 6 AM, at noon, at midnight. Используйте 'in' для месяца, года или более длительного периода: in July, in 2024, in the morning. Используйте 'on' для конкретного дня или даты: on Monday, on July 4th.

Используйте 'for', чтобы сказать, сколько что-то длится: for three hours, for two weeks. Используйте 'since', чтобы сказать, когда что-то началось: since morning, since Monday — 'since' всегда сочетается с точкой начала, а не с длиной промежутка.

examples.en: I start driving at 6 AM.
The rule changed in 2024.
I have an appointment on Monday.
I've been driving for three hours.
examples.ru: Я за рулём уже три часа.

examples.en: I've been awake since 4 AM.

mistake.wrong: I drive since three hours. I start on 6 AM.
mistake.right: I've been driving for three hours. I start at 6 AM.

why.en: 'Since' and 'for' are often confused because both can translate similarly in casual Uzbek speech — remember: for + a length of time (for 3 hours), since + a starting point (since 6 AM).
why.uz: 'Since' va 'for' koʻpincha chalkashtiriladi, chunki norasmiy oʻzbek nutqida ikkalasi ham oʻxshash tarjima qilinishi mumkin — eslab qoling: for + vaqt uzunligi (for 3 hours), since + boshlanish nuqtasi (since 6 AM).
why.ru: 'Since' и 'for' часто путают, потому что в разговорной речи на узбекском (и русском) они могут переводиться похоже — запомните: for + длина промежутка (for 3 hours), since + точка начала (since 6 AM).

q.en: 'I've been driving ___ three hours.' (a length of time)

teach: Give students the three-word cheat sheet up front: 'at' for a clock time, 'on' for a day/date, 'in' for a longer period (month, year) — this one sentence covers almost every real case they'll need.

title.en: Joining Ideas — and / but / because / so / if / when
title.uz: Fikrlarni bogʻlash — and / but / because / so / if / when
title.ru: Соединение мыслей — and / but / because / so / if / when

rule.uz: and (qoʻshish), but (qarama-qarshilik), because (sabab), so (natija), if (shart), when (vaqt) gaplarni bogʻlaydi.
rule.ru: and (добавление), but (противопоставление), because (причина), so (следствие), if (условие), when (время) связывают предложения.

en: Use 'and' to add ideas, 'but' to contrast them: "I checked the oil and the tires, but I forgot the mirrors." Use 'because' to give a reason, 'so' to give a result — they work in opposite directions: "I stopped because I was tired" (reason) vs. "I was tired, so I stopped" (result).

Use 'if' to introduce a condition and 'when' for something that's certain to happen (a fact or routine), not just possible: "If it rains, I'll slow down" (might rain) vs. "When I arrive, I'll call you" (arrival is certain).
uz: Fikrlarni qoʻshish uchun 'and', ularni qarama-qarshi qoʻyish uchun 'but' ishlating: "I checked the oil and the tires, but I forgot the mirrors." Sababni aytish uchun 'because', natijani aytish uchun 'so' ishlating — ular qarama-qarshi yoʻnalishda ishlaydi: "I stopped because I was tired" (sabab) va "I was tired, so I stopped" (natija).

Shart kiritish uchun 'if', albatta sodir boʻladigan (fakt yoki odat), shunchaki mumkin boʻlmagan narsa uchun 'when' ishlating: "If it rains, Iʼll slow down" (yomgʻir yogʻishi mumkin) va "When I arrive, Iʼll call you" (yetib borish aniq).
ru: Используйте 'and', чтобы добавлять мысли, и 'but' — чтобы противопоставлять: «I checked the oil and the tires, but I forgot the mirrors.» Используйте 'because', чтобы назвать причину, и 'so' — чтобы назвать следствие; они работают в противоположных направлениях: «I stopped because I was tired» (причина) и «I was tired, so I stopped» (следствие).

Используйте 'if' для условия и 'when' для того, что обязательно произойдёт (факт или привычка), а не просто возможно: «If it rains, I'll slow down» (может пойти дождь) и «When I arrive, I'll call you» (прибытие неизбежно).

examples.en: I checked the oil and the tires.
The load is heavy, but it's legal.
examples.ru: Груз тяжёлый, но он в рамках закона.

examples.en: I stopped because I was tired.
I was tired, so I stopped.
If it rains, I'll slow down.
examples.ru: Если пойдёт дождь, я сбавлю скорость.

mistake.wrong: Mixing up because and so, or using them both in one sentence.
mistake.right: I stopped because I was tired. OR I was tired, so I stopped. (not both)

why.en: In some languages you can use a reason-word and a result-word together in one sentence — in English, pick one: 'because' names the reason, 'so' names the result, and using both together is considered a mistake.
why.uz: Baʼzi tillarda bitta gapda sabab soʻzi va natija soʻzini birga ishlatish mumkin — ingliz tilida bittasini tanlang: 'because' sababni, 'so' natijani bildiradi, ikkalasini birga ishlatish xato hisoblanadi.
why.ru: В некоторых языках можно использовать слово-причину и слово-следствие вместе в одном предложении — в английском выберите что-то одно: 'because' называет причину, 'so' — следствие, а использование обоих вместе считается ошибкой.

q.en: 'I stopped ___ I was tired.' (giving the reason)
'I was tired, ___ I stopped.' (giving the result)
'___ it rains, I'll slow down.' (a possibility)
'___ I arrive, I'll call you.' (certain to happen)
q.uz: '___ I arrive, Iʼll call you.' (albatta sodir boʻladi)
q.ru: '___ I arrive, I'll call you.' (точно произойдёт)

teach: 'Because' and 'so' are the two truckers use constantly in real explanations (why they're late, why a load is delayed) — prioritize those two over 'if/when', which students already partly get from the conditionals unit.

title.uz: Qiyosiy va orttirma daraja — faster, the fastest
title.ru: Сравнительная и превосходная степень — faster, the fastest

rule.uz: Qisqa sifatlarga -er/-est, uzun sifatlarga more/most qoʻshiladi; baʼzilari tartibsiz (good→better→best).
rule.ru: К коротким прилагательным добавляют -er/-est, к длинным — more/most; некоторые неправильные (good→better→best).

en: For short adjectives (one syllable, or two ending in -y), add -er to compare two things and -est for the top of a group: fast → faster → the fastest, heavy → heavier → the heaviest (y changes to i).

For longer adjectives, use 'more'/'most' instead of changing the word: expensive → more expensive → the most expensive. A few common words are irregular and must be memorized: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst, far → farther → the farthest.
uz: Qisqa sifatlar uchun (bir boʻgʻin yoki -y bilan tugaydigan ikki boʻgʻin) ikki narsani solishtirish uchun -er, guruhdagi eng yaxshisi uchun -est qoʻshing: fast → faster → the fastest, heavy → heavier → the heaviest (y i ga oʻzgaradi).

Uzunroq sifatlar uchun soʻzni oʻzgartirmasdan 'more'/'most' ishlating: expensive → more expensive → the most expensive. Bir nechta keng tarqalgan soʻzlar tartibsiz va yodlanishi kerak: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst, far → farther → the farthest.
ru: К коротким прилагательным (один слог, или два слога на -y) добавьте -er, чтобы сравнить два предмета, и -est — для лучшего в группе: fast → faster → the fastest, heavy → heavier → the heaviest (y меняется на i).

Для более длинных прилагательных используйте 'more'/'most', не меняя слово: expensive → more expensive → the most expensive. Несколько частых слов неправильные, и их нужно запомнить: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst, far → farther → the farthest.

examples.en: This route is faster than the highway.
That's the biggest truck stop I've seen.
examples.uz: Bu men koʻrgan eng katta bekat.
examples.ru: Это самая большая стоянка для грузовиков, которую я видел.

examples.en: Diesel is more expensive this month.
My new truck is better than the old one.
This is the worst traffic I've seen today.
examples.uz: Bu bugun koʻrgan eng yomon tirbandlik.
examples.ru: Это самая ужасная пробка, которую я сегодня видел.

mistake.wrong: more faster, the most fastest
mistake.right: faster, the fastest

why.en: Never combine both methods on one word — a short adjective takes EITHER -er/-est OR more/most, never both together.
why.uz: Ikkala usulni bitta soʻzda hech qachon birlashtirmang — qisqa sifat YO -er/-est, YO more/most oladi, ikkalasini birga emas.
why.ru: Никогда не совмещайте оба способа в одном слове — короткое прилагательное принимает ЛИБО -er/-est, ЛИБО more/most, но не оба сразу.

q.en: 'That's ___ truck stop I've seen.' (big, top of the group)
q.uz: 'Thatʼs ___ truck stop Iʼve seen.' (big, guruhdagi eng katta)
q.ru: 'That's ___ truck stop I've seen.' (big, лучший в группе)

q.en: 'My new truck is ___ than the old one.' (good, irregular)
q.uz: 'My new truck is ___ than the old one.' (good, tartibsiz)
q.ru: 'My new truck is ___ than the old one.' (good, неправильное)

q.en: 'This is ___ traffic I've seen today.' (bad, top of the group)
q.uz: 'This is ___ traffic Iʼve seen today.' (bad, guruhdagi eng yomon)
q.ru: 'This is ___ traffic I've seen today.' (bad, худший в группе)

teach: Trucker context makes this concrete fast: compare two routes, two trucks, two loads out loud ('this route is faster', 'that load is the heaviest') — real comparisons stick better than abstract examples.

title.en: Countable & Uncountable Nouns — some / any / much / many
title.uz: Sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlar — some / any / much / many
title.ru: Исчисляемые и неисчисляемые существительные — some / any / much / many

rule.uz: Sanaladigan otlar (tire, box) many bilan, sanalmaydiganlar (fuel, traffic) much bilan ishlatiladi; raqamdan keyin koʻplik -s unutilmasin.
rule.ru: Исчисляемые (tire, box) используются с many, неисчисляемые (fuel, traffic) — с much; после числа не забывайте -s множественного числа.

en: Countable nouns can be counted one by one and have a plural form: one tire, two tires, many boxes. Uncountable nouns describe things treated as a whole, with no plural: fuel, traffic, cargo, information, equipment, weather.

Use 'many' and 'a few' with countable nouns, 'much' and 'a little' with uncountable ones: "How many tires?" / "How much fuel?" Use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in questions/negatives for both types: "I have some tools" / "Do you have any tools?"
After a number, always keep the plural -s on countable nouns — this is one you'll use constantly: three trucks, five boxes, two hours.
uz: Sanaladigan otlarni birma-bir sanash mumkin va ularning koʻplik shakli bor: one tire, two tires, many boxes. Sanalmaydigan otlar yaxlit narsa sifatida qaraladigan va koʻpligi yoʻq narsalarni bildiradi: fuel, traffic, cargo, information, equipment, weather.

Sanaladigan otlar bilan 'many' va 'a few', sanalmaydigan otlar bilan 'much' va 'a little' ishlating: "How many tires?" / "How much fuel?" Boʻlishli gaplarda 'some', savol va boʻlishsiz gaplarda 'any' ni ikkala tur uchun ishlating: "I have some tools" / "Do you have any tools?"
Raqamdan keyin sanaladigan otlarda doim koʻplik -s ni saqlang — buni doim ishlatasiz: three trucks, five boxes, two hours.
ru: Исчисляемые существительные можно посчитать по одному, и у них есть форма множественного числа: one tire, two tires, many boxes. Неисчисляемые существительные обозначают то, что воспринимается как единое целое и не имеет множественного числа: fuel, traffic, cargo, information, equipment, weather.

Используйте 'many' и 'a few' с исчисляемыми существительными, 'much' и 'a little' — с неисчисляемыми: «How many tires?» / «How much fuel?» Используйте 'some' в утвердительных предложениях и 'any' — в вопросах и отрицаниях для обоих типов: «I have some tools» / «Do you have any tools?»
После числа всегда сохраняйте -s множественного числа у исчисляемых существительных — вы будете использовать это постоянно: three trucks, five boxes, two hours.

examples.en: I have some tools in the back.
examples.ru: В кузове у меня есть несколько инструментов.

examples.en: Do you have any spare parts?
How much fuel is left?
How many tires need replacing?
We have three trucks on this route.
examples.ru: На этом маршруте у нас три грузовика.

mistake.wrong: three truck. much tires. How many fuel?
mistake.right: three trucks. many tires. How much fuel?

why.en: Uzbek usually doesn't pluralize a noun after a number (uch kitob, not "uch kitoblar"), so it's easy to forget the -s after a number in English. Also watch much (uncountable) vs. many (countable) — fuel takes much, tires take many.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida odatda raqamdan keyin ot koʻplikka qoʻyilmaydi (uch kitob, "uch kitoblar" emas), shuning uchun inglizchada raqamdan keyin -s ni unutish oson. Much (sanalmaydigan) va many (sanaladigan) ga ham eʼtibor bering: fuel bilan much, tires bilan many keladi.
why.ru: В узбекском существительное после числа обычно не ставится во множественное число (uch kitob, а не «uch kitoblar»), поэтому легко забыть -s после числа в английском. Следите и за much (неисчисляемое) и many (исчисляемое): к fuel относится much, к tires — many.

q.en: 'I have ___ tools in the back.' (positive sentence)
q.uz: 'I have ___ tools in the back.' (boʻlishli gap)
q.ru: 'I have ___ tools in the back.' (утвердительное предложение)

teach: Countable vs uncountable (many trucks vs much fuel) is the crux — have students sort a quick list of trucking nouns into two columns (countable / uncountable) as a warm-up before the explanation.

title.uz: If gaplari — qoida, ogohlantirish va maslahat
title.ru: Предложения с If — правила, предупреждения и советы

rule.uz: If + hozirgi zamon, ... + will/must/should — qoida, ogohlantirish yoki maslahat berishning eng keng tarqalgan usuli.
rule.ru: If + настоящее время, ... + will/must/should — самый частый способ сформулировать правило, предупреждение или совет.

en: This pattern is everywhere in trucking English — rules, warnings, and advice almost always use "If + present simple, ... will/must/should/can + base verb." "If you speed, you'll get a ticket." "If the light is red, you must pull in." "If you feel tired, you should stop."
Important: after 'if,' use present simple even though you're talking about the future — never 'will' in the if-part. "If it rains" is correct; "if it will rain" is not.
uz: Bu shakl yuk tashish inglizchasida hamma joyda uchraydi — qoidalar, ogohlantirishlar va maslahatlar deyarli har doim "If + Present Simple, ... will/must/should/can + asosiy feʼl" shaklida tuziladi. "If you speed, youʼll get a ticket." "If the light is red, you must pull in." "If you feel tired, you should stop."
Muhim: 'if' dan keyin kelasi zamon haqida gapirayotgan boʻlsangiz ham Present Simple ishlating — if qismida hech qachon 'will' ishlatmang. "If it rains" toʻgʻri; "if it will rain" notoʻgʻri.
ru: Эта схема встречается в английском для дальнобойщиков повсюду — правила, предупреждения и советы почти всегда строятся как «If + Present Simple, ... will/must/should/can + начальная форма глагола». «If you speed, you'll get a ticket.» «If the light is red, you must pull in.» «If you feel tired, you should stop.»
Важно: после 'if' используйте Present Simple, даже когда речь о будущем — никогда не ставьте 'will' в части с if. «If it rains» — правильно; «if it will rain» — нет.

examples.en: If you speed, you'll get a ticket.
If the light is red, you must pull in.
examples.uz: Agar chiroq qizil boʻlsa, kirishingiz shart.
examples.ru: Если свет красный, вы обязаны заехать.

examples.en: If you feel tired, you should stop.
examples.ru: Если вы устали, вам стоит остановиться.

examples.en: If your ELD malfunctions, switch to paper logs.
examples.uz: Agar ELD buzilsa, qogʻoz jurnalga oʻting.
examples.ru: Если ELD выйдет из строя, переходите на бумажные журналы.

examples.en: If the scale shows overweight, you must adjust the load.
examples.uz: Agar tarozi ortiqcha ogʻirlikni koʻrsatsa, yukni sozlashingiz kerak.
examples.ru: Если весы показывают перегруз, вы обязаны скорректировать груз.

mistake.wrong: If it will rain, I will slow down.
mistake.right: If it rains, I will slow down.

why.en: Even though the if-clause talks about the future, English never uses 'will' right after 'if.' Use present simple in the if-part, and save 'will' (or must/should/can) for the result.
why.uz: if-gap boʻlagi kelajak haqida gapirsa ham, ingliz tilida 'if' dan keyin hech qachon 'will' ishlatilmaydi. if qismida Present Simple ishlating, 'will' ni (yoki must/should/can) natija uchun saqlang.
why.ru: Хотя часть с if говорит о будущем, в английском сразу после 'if' никогда не ставят 'will'. В части с if используйте Present Simple, а 'will' (или must/should/can) оставьте для результата.

q.en: 'If the light ___ red, you must pull in.'
q.uz: 'If the light ___ red, you must pull in.'
q.ru: 'If the light ___ red, you must pull in.'

opts: If it will rain, I'll slow down.
If it rains, I'll slow down.
If it rain, I'll slow down.
If it raining, I'll slow down.

q.en: 'If your ELD malfunctions, ___ to paper logs.' (instruction)
q.uz: 'If your ELD malfunctions, ___ to paper logs.' (koʻrsatma)
q.ru: 'If your ELD malfunctions, ___ to paper logs.' (инструкция)

q.en: 'If the scale shows overweight, you ___ adjust the load.' (a rule)
q.uz: 'If the scale shows overweight, you ___ adjust the load.' (qoida)
q.ru: 'If the scale shows overweight, you ___ adjust the load.' (правило)

teach: This unit covers real safety language ('if the brakes fail, pull over') — lean into that: have students write or say their own 'if X, then Y' safety rule, which is both grammar practice and genuinely useful content.

title.uz: Koʻrsatma berish — buyruq gaplari
title.ru: Как давать указания — повелительное наклонение

rule.uz: Buyruq gaplarda ega tushiriladi va feʼl boshlangʻich shaklda ishlatiladi; iltimos uchun 'please' qoʻshiladi.
rule.ru: В повелительных предложениях подлежащее опускается, глагол стоит в начальной форме; для вежливости добавляют 'please'.

en: For instructions and commands, drop the subject and start with the base verb: "Check the mirror." "Open the trailer doors." "Wait here." Add 'please' to sound more polite, especially in professional settings: "Please wait here."

For a negative command, add 'don't' before the base verb: "Don't park here." "Don't forget your logbook." This is exactly how trainers, inspectors, and dock workers give instructions all day — it's a very common pattern in trucking English.
uz: Koʻrsatma va buyruqlar uchun egani tushiring va asosiy feʼl bilan boshlang: "Check the mirror." "Open the trailer doors." "Wait here." Muloyimroq eshitilishi uchun 'please' qoʻshing, ayniqsa professional muhitda: "Please wait here."

Boʻlishsiz buyruq uchun asosiy feʼl oldiga 'donʼt' qoʻshing: "Donʼt park here." "Donʼt forget your logbook." Oʻrgatuvchilar, inspektorlar va maydoncha ishchilari kun boʻyi aynan shunday koʻrsatma beradi — bu yuk tashish inglizchasida juda keng tarqalgan shakl.
ru: Для инструкций и команд опустите подлежащее и начните с начальной формы глагола: «Check the mirror.» «Open the trailer doors.» «Wait here.» Добавьте 'please', чтобы звучало вежливее, особенно в профессиональной обстановке: «Please wait here.»

Для отрицательной команды добавьте 'don't' перед начальной формой глагола: «Don't park here.» «Don't forget your logbook.» Именно так инструкторы, инспекторы и работники рамп отдают указания целый день — это очень частая схема в английском для дальнобойщиков.

examples.en: Check the mirror before you turn.
Please wait here.
Open the trailer doors.
Don't park in this area.
Don't forget your logbook.

mistake.wrong: You check the mirror. You don't park here.
mistake.right: Check the mirror. Don't park here.

why.en: Adding 'you' before an instruction makes it sound like a statement about someone, not a direct instruction. Real commands and instructions in English drop the subject entirely and start right with the verb.
why.uz: Koʻrsatma oldiga 'you' qoʻshish uni toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri koʻrsatma emas, kimdir haqidagi darak gap kabi eshittiradi. Ingliz tilidagi haqiqiy buyruq va koʻrsatmalar egani butunlay tushiradi va toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri feʼl bilan boshlanadi.
why.ru: Если добавить 'you' перед указанием, оно звучит как утверждение о ком-то, а не прямая инструкция. Настоящие команды и инструкции в английском полностью опускают подлежащее и сразу начинаются с глагола.

q.en: Which sounds like a direct instruction?

teach: Imperatives are how every trainer/mechanic gives instructions in this course — teach it through role-play: have the student give YOU inspection instructions ('open the hood', 'check the oil') instead of just reading examples.

title.en: Basic Word Order — Subject + Verb + Object
title.uz: Asosiy soʻz tartibi — Ega + Feʼl + Toʻldiruvchi
title.ru: Базовый порядок слов — подлежащее + глагол + дополнение

rule.uz: Ingliz tilida gap tuzilishi ega+feʼl+toʻldiruvchi (SVO) tartibida boʻladi, oʻzbek tilida esa feʼl odatda gap oxirida keladi (SOV).
rule.ru: В английском предложение строится в порядке подлежащее + глагол + дополнение (SVO), а в узбекском глагол обычно стоит в конце (SOV).

en: English sentences follow a fixed order: Subject + Verb + Object. "I (subject) drive (verb) a truck (object)." The verb comes right after the subject — almost never at the end of the sentence.

Uzbek instead puts the verb at the end (Subject-Object-Verb): "Men mashina haydayman" literally means "I truck drive." When building English sentences, the verb has to move to the middle, right after the subject. This one habit affects almost every sentence you build, so it's worth practicing on purpose.
uz: Ingliz tilidagi gaplar qatʼiy tartibga amal qiladi: Ega + Feʼl + Toʻldiruvchi. "I (ega) drive (feʼl) a truck (toʻldiruvchi)." Feʼl egadan keyin darhol keladi — deyarli hech qachon gap oxirida emas.

Oʻzbek tilida esa feʼl oxirga qoʻyiladi (Ega-Toʻldiruvchi-Feʼl): "Men mashina haydayman" soʻzma-soʻz "I truck drive" degani. Ingliz tilida gap tuzayotganda feʼl oʻrtaga, egadan keyin oʻtishi kerak. Bu odat deyarli har bir gapingizga taʼsir qiladi, shuning uchun uni ataylab mashq qilishga arziydi.
ru: Английские предложения следуют жёсткому порядку: подлежащее + глагол + дополнение. «I (подлежащее) drive (глагол) a truck (дополнение).» Глагол стоит сразу после подлежащего — почти никогда не в конце предложения.

В узбекском глагол ставится в конец (подлежащее-дополнение-глагол): «Men mashina haydayman» буквально означает «Я грузовик вожу». Когда вы строите английские предложения, глагол должен переместиться в середину — прямо после подлежащего. Эта привычка влияет почти на каждое предложение, поэтому стоит тренировать её сознательно.

examples.en: I drive a truck.
She checks the engine every morning.
examples.uz: U har kuni ertalab dvigatelni tekshiradi.

examples.en: We deliver furniture to Phoenix.
The officer checked my documents.
Dispatch sent me a new load.

mistake.wrong: I truck drive. Furniture to Phoenix deliver.
mistake.right: I drive a truck. I deliver furniture to Phoenix.

why.en: Because Uzbek puts the verb last, it feels natural to build English sentences the same way. Always place the verb right after the subject, not at the end.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida feʼl oxirida boʻlgani uchun, ingliz gaplarini ham shunday tuzish tabiiy tuyuladi. Feʼlni doim egadan keyin qoʻying, oxirga emas.
why.ru: Поскольку в узбекском глагол стоит в конце, кажется естественным строить английские предложения так же. Всегда ставьте глагол сразу после подлежащего, а не в конце.

q.en: Put in order: 'a truck / I / drive'
q.ru: Расставьте по порядку: 'a truck / I / drive'

q.en: Put in order: 'the engine / checks / she / every morning'
q.uz: Tartibga soling: 'the engine / checks / she / every morning'
q.ru: Расставьте по порядку: 'the engine / checks / she / every morning'

opts: She checks the engine every morning.
She the engine checks every morning.
Every morning she the engine checks.
Checks she the engine every morning.

q.en: Which sentence has correct English word order?
q.uz: Qaysi gapda inglizcha soʻz tartibi toʻgʻri?
q.ru: В каком предложении верный английский порядок слов?

q.en: 'Dispatch ___ me a new load.' (correct verb position)
q.uz: 'Dispatch ___ me a new load.' (feʼlning toʻgʻri oʻrni)
q.ru: 'Dispatch ___ me a new load.' (верное место глагола)

q.en: Where does the verb usually go in an English sentence?
q.uz: Ingliz gapida feʼl odatda qayerda turadi?
q.ru: Где обычно стоит глагол в английском предложении?

teach: Basic S-V-O order differs from Uzbek's S-O-V, so this unit is foundational — if a student keeps making mistakes elsewhere, it's often actually a word-order problem underneath, so revisit this unit before assuming it's a tense or vocabulary issue.

title.uz: Ega olmoshlari va egalik shakli — I/my, you/your...
title.ru: Личные местоимения и притяжательные формы — I/my, you/your...

rule.uz: Subject olmoshlari (I, you, he...) ega oʻrnida, egalik olmoshlari (my, your, his...) esa kimga tegishli ekanini bildiradi.
rule.ru: Личные местоимения (I, you, he...) заменяют подлежащее, а притяжательные (my, your, his...) показывают, кому что принадлежит.

en: Subject pronouns replace the doer of the action: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. "He checks the load" (not "Him checks the load").

Possessive adjectives show who something belongs to, and go right before a noun: my truck, your license, his trailer, her route, its engine, our company, their schedule. Don't confuse them with subject pronouns — "I truck" is wrong; you need "my truck."
For a person's name or a noun, add 's to show possession: the driver's log, the company's policy, Aziz's truck.
uz: Ega olmoshlari harakatni bajaruvchini almashtiradi: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. "He checks the load" ("Him checks the load" emas).

Egalik sifatlari biror narsa kimga tegishli ekanini koʻrsatadi va otdan oldin keladi: my truck, your license, his trailer, her route, its engine, our company, their schedule. Ularni ega olmoshlari bilan chalkashtirmang — "I truck" notoʻgʻri; "my truck" kerak.
Odam ismi yoki ot uchun tegishlilikni koʻrsatish uchun 's qoʻshing: the driverʼs log, the companyʼs policy, Azizʼs truck.
ru: Личные местоимения заменяют того, кто совершает действие: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. «He checks the load» (а не «Him checks the load»).

Притяжательные прилагательные показывают, кому что-то принадлежит, и стоят прямо перед существительным: my truck, your license, his trailer, her route, its engine, our company, their schedule. Не путайте их с личными местоимениями — «I truck» неправильно; нужно «my truck».
Для имени человека или существительного добавьте 's, чтобы показать принадлежность: the driver's log, the company's policy, Aziz's truck.

examples.en: My truck needs an oil change.
Is this your logbook?
Her route goes through Denver.
The driver's log was up to date.
Our company covers fuel costs.
examples.ru: Наша компания покрывает расходы на топливо.

mistake.wrong: Me truck. This is I logbook.
mistake.right: My truck. This is my logbook.

why.en: It's easy to reach for the subject pronoun (I, he, they) even when you need the possessive form (my, his, their) right before a noun. If a noun follows, use the possessive form.
why.uz: Otdan oldin egalik shakli (my, his, their) kerak boʻlganda ham ega olmoshiga (I, he, they) qoʻl choʻzish oson. Agar ot kelsa, egalik shaklidan foydalaning.
why.ru: Легко потянуться к личному местоимению (I, he, they), когда нужна притяжательная форма (my, his, their) прямо перед существительным. Если дальше идёт существительное, используйте притяжательную форму.

q.en: '___ truck needs an oil change.' (belongs to me)
q.uz: '___ truck needs an oil change.' (menga tegishli)
q.ru: '___ truck needs an oil change.' (принадлежит мне)

q.en: '___ route goes through Denver.' (belongs to her)
Correct possessive for a noun: 'the driver ___ log'
q.uz: Ot uchun toʻgʻri egalik shakli: 'the driver ___ log'
q.ru: Правильная притяжательная форма для существительного: 'the driver ___ log'

q.en: '___ company covers fuel costs.' (belongs to us)

teach: Confusing 'your'/'you're' or 'their'/'there'/'they're' in writing is common even at higher levels — if you're teaching literacy alongside speaking, spend extra time on the written forms specifically.

title.uz: Sonlar — mikdor va tartib sonlar
title.ru: Числа — количественные и порядковые

rule.uz: Cardinal sonlar sanash uchun (one, two, three), ordinal sonlar esa tartib uchun (first, second, third) ishlatiladi.
rule.ru: Количественные числительные нужны для счёта (one, two, three), порядковые — для порядка (first, second, third).

en: Cardinal numbers count things: one, two, three, twenty, eighty thousand. Use them for weights, quantities, and most numbers: "eighty thousand pounds," "three trucks."

Ordinal numbers show order or position: first, second, third, fourth... fifth, and are used for dates and exits: "March fifth" (not "March five"), "take the third exit." Most ordinals add -th to the cardinal number, but first, second, and third are irregular.
For large numbers, break them into groups: 80,000 = "eighty thousand." 1,200 = "one thousand two hundred" or "twelve hundred."
uz: Miqdor sonlar narsalarni sanaydi: one, two, three, twenty, eighty thousand. Ularni ogʻirlik, miqdor va aksariyat sonlar uchun ishlating: "eighty thousand pounds," "three trucks."

Tartib sonlar tartib yoki oʻrinni koʻrsatadi: first, second, third, fourth... fifth va sanalar hamda chiqishlar uchun ishlatiladi: "March fifth" ("March five" emas), "take the third exit." Koʻpchilik tartib sonlar miqdor songa -th qoʻshish bilan hosil boʻladi, lekin first, second va third tartibsiz.
Katta sonlarni guruhlarga boʻling: 80,000 = "eighty thousand." 1,200 = "one thousand two hundred" yoki "twelve hundred."
ru: Количественные числительные считают предметы: one, two, three, twenty, eighty thousand. Используйте их для веса, количества и большинства чисел: «eighty thousand pounds», «three trucks».

Порядковые числительные показывают порядок или место: first, second, third, fourth... fifth — их используют для дат и съездов: «March fifth» (а не «March five»), «take the third exit». Большинство порядковых образуются добавлением -th к количественному числительному, но first, second и third — исключения.
Большие числа разбивайте на группы: 80,000 = «eighty thousand». 1,200 = «one thousand two hundred» или «twelve hundred».

examples.en: The gross weight is eighty thousand pounds.
Take the third exit.
My delivery is on March fifth.
examples.uz: Mening yetkazib berishim mart oyining beshinchisida.

examples.en: This is my first trip to Chicago.
examples.ru: Это мой первый рейс в Чикаго.

examples.en: We have twelve hundred miles left.

mistake.wrong: March five. The two exit.
mistake.right: March fifth. The second exit.

why.en: Dates and ordered positions (exits, floors, anniversaries) use ordinal numbers (fifth, second), not cardinal numbers (five, two) — this trips up almost every English learner at first.
why.uz: Sanalar va tartibli oʻrinlar (chiqishlar, qavatlar, yubileylar) miqdor sonlar (five, two) emas, tartib sonlar (fifth, second) ishlatadi — bu boshida deyarli har bir ingliz tili oʻrganuvchini adashtiradi.
why.ru: Даты и порядковые позиции (съезды, этажи, годовщины) требуют порядковых числительных (fifth, second), а не количественных (five, two) — на этом сначала спотыкается почти каждый изучающий английский.

q.en: Which is the ordinal form of 'two'?

teach: Ordinal numbers (1st, 2nd, 3rd) matter for real trucking situations — exit numbers, dates, addresses — more than students expect; don't treat this as a 'beginner' unit to rush through.

title.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamon — tajriba va yaqinda sodir boʻlgan voqealar
title.ru: Present Perfect — опыт и недавние события

rule.uz: have/has + oʻtgan zamon shakli (participle) — tajriba yoki hozirgacha davom etayotgan vaqtni bildiradi.
rule.ru: have/has + причастие прошедшего времени (participle) — обозначает опыт или время, длящееся до настоящего.

en: Use have/has + past participle to talk about life experience (not a specific time), or something that started in the past and connects to now: "I have driven for 10 years" (still true now). "Have you ever driven a tanker?" (at any point in your life).

This is different from past simple, which names a finished, specific time: "I drove to Dallas yesterday" (done, specific day) vs. "I have driven to Dallas many times" (experience, no specific day named).
Many past participles are irregular and different from the past simple form: drive → drove → driven, see → saw → seen, go → went → gone, do → did → done.
uz: Hayotiy tajriba (aniq vaqtsiz) yoki oʻtmishda boshlangan va hozirga bogʻlangan narsa haqida gapirish uchun have/has + oʻtgan zamon sifatdoshidan foydalaning: "I have driven for 10 years" (hozir ham toʻgʻri). "Have you ever driven a tanker?" (hayotingizning istalgan paytida).
Bu Past Simpleʼdan farq qiladi, u tugagan, aniq vaqtni bildiradi: "I drove to Dallas yesterday" (tugagan, aniq kun) va "I have driven to Dallas many times" (tajriba, aniq kun aytilmagan).
Koʻplab oʻtgan zamon sifatdoshlari tartibsiz va Past Simple shaklidan farq qiladi: drive → drove → driven, see → saw → seen, go → went → gone, do → did → done.
ru: Используйте have/has + причастие прошедшего времени, чтобы говорить о жизненном опыте (без конкретного времени) или о том, что началось в прошлом и связано с настоящим: «I have driven for 10 years» (это верно и сейчас). «Have you ever driven a tanker?» (в любой момент вашей жизни).

Это отличается от Past Simple, которое называет завершённое, конкретное время: «I drove to Dallas yesterday» (сделано, конкретный день) и «I have driven to Dallas many times» (опыт, конкретный день не указан).
Многие причастия прошедшего времени неправильные и отличаются от формы Past Simple: drive → drove → driven, see → saw → seen, go → went → gone, do → did → done.

examples.en: I have driven for ten years.
Have you ever driven a tanker?
I have already inspected the truck.
She has worked here since 2020.
We haven't received the new schedule yet.
examples.ru: Мы ещё не получили новое расписание.

mistake.wrong: I drive trucks for ten years. I never drove a tanker (meaning: in my whole life).
mistake.right: I have driven trucks for ten years. I have never driven a tanker.

why.en: When talking about experience up to now, or something that started in the past and continues, English needs have/has + past participle — past simple alone only works for a specific, finished time.
why.uz: Hozirgacha boʻlgan tajriba yoki oʻtmishda boshlanib davom etayotgan narsa haqida gapirganda, ingliz tilida have/has + oʻtgan zamon sifatdoshi kerak — faqat Past Simple aniq, tugagan vaqt uchungina ishlaydi.
why.ru: Когда вы говорите об опыте до настоящего момента или о том, что началось в прошлом и продолжается, в английском нужен have/has + причастие прошедшего времени — одно только Past Simple подходит лишь для конкретного завершённого времени.

q.ru: 'I ___ (drive) for ten years.' (это верно и сейчас)

q.en: Which sentence describes a specific finished time?
q.uz: Qaysi gap aniq tugagan vaqtni tasvirlaydi?
q.ru: Какое предложение описывает конкретное завершённое время?

opts: I have driven to Dallas many times.
I have never driven a tanker.

teach: This is one of the hardest tenses for Uzbek speakers, since Uzbek doesn't distinguish 'I have driven' (experience, unspecified time) from 'I drove' (a specific past time) the same way — contrast the two directly using the same verb in both forms.

title.uz: Oʻtgan davomli zamon — nima sodir boʻlayotgan edi
title.ru: Past Continuous — что происходило

rule.uz: was/were + feʼl-ing — oʻtgan bir paytda davom etayotgan harakatni bildiradi, koʻpincha boshqa qisqa harakat uni toʻxtatadi.
