rule.ru: was/were + глагол с -ing обозначает действие, которое длилось в определённый момент прошлого, — часто его прерывает другое, короткое действие.

en: Use was/were + verb-ing to describe an action that was already in progress at a specific point in the past — very useful for describing what was happening right before or during an incident: "I was driving when the deer ran into the road."

This pairs naturally with the past simple: the past continuous sets the scene (the longer action in progress), and the past simple names the shorter action that interrupted it. "I was checking the brakes when the phone rang."
uz: Oʻtmishning aniq bir paytida allaqachon davom etayotgan harakatni tasvirlash uchun was/were + feʼl-ing ishlating — voqeadan oldin yoki voqea paytida nima sodir boʻlayotganini tasvirlash uchun juda foydali: "I was driving when the deer ran into the road."

Bu Past Simple bilan tabiiy juftlashadi: Past Continuous manzarani chizadi (davom etayotgan uzunroq harakat), Past Simple esa uni toʻxtatgan qisqaroq harakatni nomlaydi. "I was checking the brakes when the phone rang."
ru: Используйте was/were + глагол с -ing, чтобы описать действие, которое уже шло в определённый момент прошлого, — это очень полезно для описания того, что происходило прямо перед происшествием или во время него: «I was driving when the deer ran into the road.»

Это естественно сочетается с Past Simple: Past Continuous задаёт сцену (более длительное действие в процессе), а Past Simple называет более короткое действие, которое его прервало. «I was checking the brakes when the phone rang.»

examples.en: I was driving when the deer ran into the road.
examples.uz: Kiyik yoʻlga chiqqanda men haydab ketayotgan edim.
examples.ru: Я ехал, когда олень выбежал на дорогу.

examples.en: We were waiting at the dock when the call came.
examples.uz: Qoʻngʻiroq kelganda biz maydonchada kutayotgan edik.
examples.ru: Мы ждали на рампе, когда раздался звонок.

examples.en: I was checking the brakes when the phone rang.
examples.ru: Я проверял тормоза, когда зазвонил телефон.

examples.en: She was sleeping in the berth during the stop.
examples.uz: Toʻxtash paytida u uxlash boʻlimida uxlayotgan edi.
examples.ru: Во время остановки она спала на спальном месте.

examples.en: It was raining heavily when the accident happened.
examples.uz: Avariya sodir boʻlganda kuchli yomgʻir yogʻayotgan edi.
examples.ru: Когда произошла авария, шёл сильный дождь.

mistake.wrong: I drove when the deer ran into the road. (losing the 'in progress' meaning)
mistake.right: I was driving when the deer ran into the road.

why.en: Using plain past simple for both actions loses the important distinction between the longer background action (was driving) and the sudden interrupting action (ran) — both details matter in an incident report.
why.uz: Ikkala harakat uchun oddiy Past Simple ishlatish uzunroq fon harakati (was driving) va toʻsatdan toʻxtatgan harakat (ran) oʻrtasidagi muhim farqni yoʻqotadi — hodisa hisobotida ikkala tafsilot ham muhim.
why.ru: Если использовать простое Past Simple для обоих действий, теряется важное различие между более длительным фоновым действием (was driving) и внезапным прерывающим действием (ran) — в отчёте о происшествии важны обе детали.

q.en: 'I ___ (drive) when the deer ran into the road.'
q.uz: 'I ___ (drive) when the deer ran into the road.'
q.ru: 'I ___ (drive) when the deer ran into the road.'

q.en: 'We ___ (wait) at the dock when the call came.'
q.uz: 'We ___ (wait) at the dock when the call came.'
q.ru: 'We ___ (wait) at the dock when the call came.'

q.en: 'I was checking the brakes when the phone ___ (ring).'
q.uz: 'I was checking the brakes when the phone ___ (ring).'
q.ru: 'I was checking the brakes when the phone ___ (ring).'

q.en: Which action is the 'in progress' one in: 'She was sleeping when dispatch called'?
q.uz: 'She was sleeping when dispatch called' gapida qaysi harakat 'davom etayotgan'?
q.ru: Какое действие 'в процессе' в: 'She was sleeping when dispatch called'?

teach: Pair this with past-simple in the same session: 'I was driving when the tire blew' — past continuous sets the scene, past simple is the interrupting event. This pairing is common in real incident storytelling.

title.uz: Xushmuomala va bilvosita savollar
title.ru: Вежливые и косвенные вопросы

rule.uz: Bilvosita savollarda gap tartibi toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri savoldagidek emas, balki oddiy gap tartibida boʻladi.
rule.ru: В косвенных вопросах порядок слов такой же, как в обычном утверждении, а не как в прямом вопросе.

en: For a more polite or formal question, wrap it inside a phrase like "Could you tell me..." or "Do you know..." This softens the question, which is useful with customers, officers, or anyone you want to sound extra respectful toward.

The tricky part: inside the polite wrapper, word order goes back to normal STATEMENT order (subject before verb) — not the inverted order of a direct question. Direct: "Where is the office?" Polite/indirect: "Could you tell me where the office is?" (not "...where is the office?").
uz: Muloyimroq yoki rasmiyroq savol uchun uni "Could you tell me..." yoki "Do you know..." kabi ibora ichiga joylashtiring. Bu savolni yumshatadi va mijozlar, ofitserlar yoki alohida hurmat bildirmoqchi boʻlgan har qanday odam bilan foydali.

Qiyin joyi: muloyim oʻram ichida soʻz tartibi oddiy DARAK gap tartibiga (ega feʼldan oldin) qaytadi — toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri savolning teskari tartibiga emas. Toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri: "Where is the office?" Muloyim/bilvosita: "Could you tell me where the office is?" ("...where is the office?" emas).
ru: Чтобы вопрос прозвучал вежливее или официальнее, «заверните» его во фразу вроде «Could you tell me...» или «Do you know...». Это смягчает вопрос и полезно в общении с клиентами, офицерами и всеми, к кому вы хотите проявить особое уважение.

Сложность в том, что внутри вежливой обёртки порядок слов возвращается к обычному порядку УТВЕРЖДЕНИЯ (подлежащее перед глаголом) — а не к обратному порядку прямого вопроса. Прямой: «Where is the office?» Вежливый/косвенный: «Could you tell me where the office is?» (а не «...where is the office?»).

examples.en: Could you tell me where the office is?
Do you know if the dock is open?
examples.ru: Вы не знаете, открыта ли рампа?

examples.en: Could you tell me what time the gate opens?
examples.uz: Darvoza soat nechada ochilishini ayta olasizmi?
examples.ru: Не подскажете, во сколько открываются ворота?

examples.en: Do you know where I can park overnight?

examples.en: Could you tell me how long the delay will be?
examples.uz: Kechikish qancha davom etishini ayta olasizmi?
examples.ru: Не подскажете, как долго продлится задержка?

mistake.wrong: Could you tell me where is the office?
mistake.right: Could you tell me where the office is?

why.en: It's natural to keep the inverted word order from a direct question, but inside a polite wrapper like 'Could you tell me...' the rest of the sentence goes back to normal subject-then-verb order.
why.uz: Toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri savoldagi teskari soʻz tartibini saqlash tabiiy, lekin 'Could you tell me...' kabi muloyim oʻram ichida gapning qolgan qismi oddiy ega-keyin-feʼl tartibiga qaytadi.
why.ru: Естественно сохранять обратный порядок слов из прямого вопроса, но внутри вежливой обёртки вроде 'Could you tell me...' остальная часть предложения возвращается к обычному порядку «подлежащее, потом глагол».

title.uz: Might / may / could — ehtimollik
title.ru: Might / May / Could — возможность

rule.uz: Might, may va could hozirgi yoki kelasi vaqtdagi ehtimollikni, taxminni bildiradi — ruxsat yoki qobiliyat emas.
rule.ru: Might, may и could выражают возможность или предположение о настоящем или будущем — а не разрешение или умение.

en: Use might, may, or could when you're not sure about something and you're making a guess: "It might rain later." "The delay could be traffic." "He may already be at the dock." All three are pretty similar in meaning here — a genuine guess about present or future.

Don't confuse this with 'can,' which usually states a general ability or fact, not a specific guess: "It can rain in spring" (a general fact about spring) vs. "It might rain today" (a specific guess about today's weather).
uz: Biror narsaga ishonchingiz komil boʻlmaganda va taxmin qilganda might, may yoki could ishlating: "It might rain later." "The delay could be traffic." "He may already be at the dock." Bu yerda uchalasi ham maʼno jihatidan ancha oʻxshash — hozirgi yoki kelasi vaqt haqidagi haqiqiy taxmin.

Buni 'can' bilan chalkashtirmang, u odatda aniq taxmin emas, umumiy qobiliyat yoki faktni bildiradi: "It can rain in spring" (bahor haqidagi umumiy fakt) va "It might rain today" (bugungi ob-havo haqidagi aniq taxmin).
ru: Используйте might, may или could, когда вы в чём-то не уверены и делаете предположение: «It might rain later.» «The delay could be traffic.» «He may already be at the dock.» Все три здесь по смыслу довольно близки — настоящее предположение о настоящем или будущем.

Не путайте это с 'can', которое обычно выражает общее умение или факт, а не конкретное предположение: «It can rain in spring» (общий факт о весне) и «It might rain today» (конкретное предположение о сегодняшней погоде).

examples.en: It might rain later today.
The delay could be traffic.
He may already be at the dock.
We might need to reroute.
examples.uz: Bizga marshrutni oʻzgartirish kerak boʻlishi mumkin.

examples.en: The scale could be closed tonight.
examples.uz: Tarozi bugun kechqurun yopiq boʻlishi mumkin.
examples.ru: Сегодня вечером весы могут быть закрыты.

mistake.wrong: It can rain today. (as a specific guess about today)
mistake.right: It might rain today.

why.en: 'Can' usually describes a general possibility or fact, while 'might/may/could' express a specific, uncertain guess about one particular situation — mixing them up changes how confident or general your statement sounds.
why.uz: 'Can' odatda umumiy imkoniyat yoki faktni tasvirlaydi, 'might/may/could' esa bitta aniq vaziyat haqidagi noaniq taxminni ifodalaydi — ularni aralashtirish gapingiz qanchalik ishonchli yoki umumiy eshitilishini oʻzgartiradi.
why.ru: 'Can' обычно описывает общую возможность или факт, а 'might/may/could' выражают конкретное, неуверенное предположение об одной ситуации — если их перепутать, меняется степень уверенности или обобщённости вашей фразы.

q.en: Which expresses a general fact, not a specific guess?
q.uz: Qaysi biri aniq taxmin emas, umumiy faktni ifodalaydi?
q.ru: Какое предложение выражает общий факт, а не конкретное предположение?

teach: Might/may/could for possibility is subtle even for advanced learners — keep this unit light and example-heavy rather than rule-heavy; recognizing it in context (weather/traffic reports) matters more than producing it perfectly.

title.uz: Haydovchilar ishlatadigan feʼl+old koʻmakchi birikmalar
title.ru: Фразовые глаголы, которые используют дальнобойщики

rule.uz: Feʼl+old koʻmakchi birikmasi (phrasal verb) alohida maʼnoga ega boʻladi — soʻzma-soʻz tarjima qilib boʻlmaydi.
rule.ru: Фразовый глагол (глагол + частица) приобретает отдельное значение — его нельзя перевести слово в слово.

en: A phrasal verb combines a verb with a small word (up, off, over, down...) to make a new meaning that you often can't guess from the verb alone. Trucking English uses these constantly: pull over (stop the vehicle), check in (arrive and register), load up (put cargo in), fill up (add fuel), break down (stop working, mechanically), pick up (collect cargo), drop off (deliver cargo).
These can't be translated word-by-word into Uzbek — the meaning belongs to the whole phrase, so it's best to learn each one as a single vocabulary item, the same way you'd learn any other word.
uz: Frazali feʼl — feʼlning kichik soʻz (up, off, over, down...) bilan birikmasi boʻlib, koʻpincha faqat feʼlning oʻzidan taxmin qilib boʻlmaydigan yangi maʼno beradi. Yuk tashish inglizchasida bular doim ishlatiladi: pull over (mashinani toʻxtatish), check in (kelib roʻyxatdan oʻtish), load up (yukni ortish), fill up (yoqilgʻi quyish), break down (texnika ishlamay qolishi), pick up (yukni olish), drop off (yukni yetkazish).
Bularni oʻzbek tiliga soʻzma-soʻz tarjima qilib boʻlmaydi — maʼno butun iboraga tegishli, shuning uchun har birini boshqa istalgan soʻz kabi bitta lugʻat birligi sifatida oʻrganish eng yaxshisi.
ru: Фразовый глагол — это сочетание глагола с маленьким словом (up, off, over, down...), которое даёт новое значение, часто не угадываемое по одному глаголу. В английском для дальнобойщиков такие глаголы встречаются постоянно: pull over (остановить машину), check in (прибыть и зарегистрироваться), load up (загрузить груз), fill up (заправиться), break down (сломаться, о технике), pick up (забрать груз), drop off (доставить груз).
Их нельзя перевести на узбекский (или русский) слово в слово — значение принадлежит всей фразе, поэтому лучше учить каждый как одно слово из словаря, как любое другое слово.

examples.en: Pull over at the next exit.
examples.ru: Съезжайте на обочину на следующем съезде.

examples.en: Check in at the front office first.
We need to load up before noon.
Fill up before you hit the highway.
examples.ru: Заправьтесь, прежде чем выезжать на трассу.

examples.en: The truck broke down near mile marker 90.

mistake.wrong: Translating 'pull over' or 'break down' word-by-word into Uzbek and back.
mistake.right: Learn the whole phrase as one unit: pull over = stop the vehicle; break down = stop working.

why.en: Phrasal verbs are a known trap for every English learner, not just Uzbek speakers — the individual words often give no hint at all about the combined meaning, so they have to be memorized as complete units.
why.uz: Frazali feʼllar nafaqat oʻzbekzabonlar, balki har bir ingliz tili oʻrganuvchi uchun maʼlum tuzoq — alohida soʻzlar koʻpincha birikma maʼnosi haqida hech qanday ishora bermaydi, shuning uchun ularni toʻliq birlik sifatida yodlash kerak.
why.ru: Фразовые глаголы — известная ловушка для всех, кто учит английский, а не только для узбекоговорящих: отдельные слова часто ничего не подсказывают о значении сочетания, поэтому их нужно запоминать как цельные единицы.

opts: Stop the vehicle at the side

teach: See the notes on 'Phrasal Verbs Truckers Use II' for a shared drill idea — mime or act out each phrasal verb while saying it; the physical action anchors the meaning better than a definition does.

title.uz: Sana va vaqtni aytish
title.ru: Как называть даты и время

rule.uz: Sana aytishda tartib sonlar (fifth), vaqt aytishda soat va daqiqalar (six thirty) ishlatiladi.
rule.ru: Для дат используют порядковые числительные (fifth), для времени — часы и минуты (six thirty).

en: Say clock times as hour + minutes: 6:30 = "six thirty," 7:15 = "seven fifteen." For the top and bottom of the hour, you can also say "half past six" (6:30) or "a quarter past seven" (7:15). Always add AM or PM when it's not obvious from context.
Say dates with the month first, then the ordinal day: March 5th = "March fifth." You can also say "the fifth of March." Years are usually split in pairs: 2024 = "twenty twenty-four."
uz: Soat vaqtini soat + daqiqa deb ayting: 6:30 = "six thirty," 7:15 = "seven fifteen." Toʻliq va yarim soat uchun "half past six" (6:30) yoki "a quarter past seven" (7:15) ham deyish mumkin. Kontekstdan aniq boʻlmasa, doim AM yoki PM qoʻshing.

Sanalarni avval oy, keyin tartib sonli kun bilan ayting: March 5th = "March fifth." Shuningdek, "the fifth of March" ham deyish mumkin. Yillar odatda ikkita juftlikka boʻlinadi: 2024 = "twenty twenty-four."
ru: Время по часам называйте как час + минуты: 6:30 = «six thirty», 7:15 = «seven fifteen». Для целого и половины часа можно также сказать «half past six» (6:30) или «a quarter past seven» (7:15). Всегда добавляйте AM или PM, если это не очевидно из контекста.
Даты называйте, сначала указывая месяц, а затем порядковый день: March 5th = «March fifth». Можно сказать и «the fifth of March». Годы обычно произносят парами цифр: 2024 = «twenty twenty-four».

examples.en: My appointment is at six thirty AM.
examples.ru: Моя встреча в шесть тридцать утра.

examples.en: The dock closes at a quarter past five.
examples.ru: Рампа закрывается в пятнадцать минут шестого.

examples.en: Delivery is scheduled for March fifth.
examples.uz: Yetkazib berish mart oyining beshinchisiga rejalashtirilgan.

examples.en: I started this job in twenty twenty-two.
examples.ru: Я начал эту работу в две тысячи двадцать втором году.

examples.en: We leave at noon and arrive by six PM.
examples.uz: Peshinda joʻnab, kechqurun soat oltigacha yetib boramiz.
examples.ru: Мы выезжаем в полдень и прибываем к шести вечера.

mistake.wrong: March five. Twenty two thousand twenty-four.
mistake.right: March fifth. Twenty twenty-four.

why.en: Dates use ordinal numbers (fifth, not five), and years are almost always split into two pairs of digits when spoken (twenty twenty-four), not read as one long number.
why.uz: Sanalarda tartib sonlar ishlatiladi (five emas, fifth), yillar esa ogʻzaki aytilganda deyarli har doim ikkita raqam juftligiga boʻlinadi (twenty twenty-four), bitta uzun son sifatida oʻqilmaydi.
why.ru: Даты используют порядковые числительные (fifth, а не five), а годы почти всегда произносят как две пары цифр (twenty twenty-four), а не как одно длинное число.

q.en: How do you usually say the year 2024?

title.en: Reported Speech — Relaying What Someone Said
title.uz: Koʻchirma gap — kimningdir aytganini yetkazish
title.ru: Косвенная речь — как передать чьи-то слова

rule.uz: Kimningdir gapini oʻz soʻzlaring bilan aytib berganda, feʼl zamoni odatda bir bosqich orqaga suriladi (said/told).
rule.ru: Когда вы пересказываете чьи-то слова, время глагола обычно сдвигается на шаг назад (said/told).

en: When you relay what someone said — reporting to dispatch what an officer told you, or telling a coworker what dispatch said — use 'said' (no listener named) or 'told' (must name who was told): "He said (that) the road was closed." "She told me to wait here."

The verb tense usually shifts one step into the past: "is" becomes "was," "will" becomes "would," present simple becomes past simple. Direct: "The road is closed." Reported: "He said the road was closed."
For a reported command or instruction, use told + person + to + base verb: "She told me to wait here" (not "She told me that I should wait").
uz: Kimningdir aytganini yetkazganda — ofitser sizga nima deganini dispetcherga aytganda yoki dispetcher nima deganini hamkasbingizga aytganda — 'said' (tinglovchi nomi aytilmaydi) yoki 'told' (kimga aytilgani nomlanishi shart) ishlating: "He said (that) the road was closed." "She told me to wait here."

Feʼl zamoni odatda bir qadam oʻtmishga suriladi: "is" "was" ga, "will" "would" ga, Present Simple Past Simpleʼga aylanadi. Toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri: "The road is closed." Koʻchirma: "He said the road was closed."
Koʻchirma buyruq yoki koʻrsatma uchun told + shaxs + to + asosiy feʼldan foydalaning: "She told me to wait here" ("She told me that I should wait" emas).
ru: Когда вы пересказываете чьи-то слова — сообщаете диспетчеру, что вам сказал офицер, или рассказываете коллеге, что сказал диспетчер, — используйте 'said' (слушатель не называется) или 'told' (слушателя нужно назвать): «He said (that) the road was closed.» «She told me to wait here.»

Время глагола обычно сдвигается на шаг в прошлое: «is» становится «was», «will» становится «would», Present Simple становится Past Simple. Прямая речь: «The road is closed.» Косвенная: «He said the road was closed.»
Для пересказа команды или инструкции используйте told + человек + to + начальная форма глагола: «She told me to wait here» (а не «She told me that I should wait»).

examples.en: He said the road was closed.
She told me to wait here.
examples.uz: U menga shu yerda kutishni aytdi.

examples.en: Dispatch said they would call back.
The officer told me to pull over.
examples.ru: Офицер сказал мне съехать на обочину.

examples.en: He said he had already inspected the trailer.
examples.ru: Он сказал, что уже осмотрел прицеп.

mistake.wrong: She told that I should wait. He said me the road is closed.
mistake.right: She told me to wait. He said the road was closed.

why.en: 'Said' never takes a listener directly after it (no 'said me') — use 'told' instead when you name who was spoken to. And remember the tense usually shifts back one step: 'is' becomes 'was.'
why.uz: 'Said' dan keyin tinglovchi toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri kelmaydi ('said me' yoʻq) — kimga aytilganini nomlasangiz, 'told' ishlating. Va zamon odatda bir qadam orqaga surilishini eslab qoling: 'is' 'was' boʻladi.
why.ru: После 'said' слушатель напрямую не называется (нельзя 'said me') — если вы называете, кому говорили, используйте 'told'. И помните, что время обычно сдвигается назад на шаг: 'is' становится 'was'.

q.en: 'He ___ the road was closed.' (no listener named)
q.ru: 'He ___ the road was closed.' (слушатель не назван)

q.en: Direct: 'The dock is open.' Reported: 'He said the dock ___ open.'
q.uz: Toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri: 'The dock is open.' Koʻchirma: 'He said the dock ___ open.'
q.ru: Прямая речь: 'The dock is open.' Косвенная: 'He said the dock ___ open.'

opts: He said me the truck was ready.
He told me the truck was ready.
He told that the truck was ready.
He said that me the truck was ready.

q.uz: 'Dispatch said they ___ call back.' (kelasi zamon, koʻchirma)
q.ru: 'Dispatch said they ___ call back.' (будущее, косвенная речь)

teach: This is advanced and genuinely hard — only introduce it once present/past tenses feel solid. Real use case: relaying what a dispatcher said ('He said the load was ready') comes up constantly on the job, so it's worth the difficulty.

title.en: Gerunds vs. Infinitives — Verb + -ing vs Verb + to
title.uz: Gerundiy va infinitiv — feʼl + -ing yoki feʼl + to
title.ru: Герундий и инфинитив — глагол + -ing или глагол + to

rule.uz: Baʼzi feʼllardan keyin boshqa feʼl -ing bilan, baʼzilaridan keyin esa 'to' bilan keladi — buni qoida bilan emas, har bir feʼl uchun alohida yodlash kerak.
rule.ru: После одних глаголов другой глагол ставится с -ing, после других — с «to»; это не выводится из правила, а запоминается для каждого глагола отдельно.

en: Some verbs are followed by another verb ending in -ing (a gerund): enjoy, avoid, finish, practice, keep on. "I enjoy driving at night." "We finished loading the trailer." Other verbs are followed by "to" + the base verb (an infinitive): want, need, plan, decide, agree. "She wants to become an owner-operator."

There's no shortcut rule for which is which — you have to learn each verb individually, the same way you'd learn a new vocabulary word. A short list of the most common ones is enough to cover most real trucking conversation.
uz: Baʼzi feʼllardan keyin -ing bilan tugaydigan boshqa feʼl keladi (gerundiy): enjoy, avoid, finish, practice, keep on. «I enjoy driving at night.» «We finished loading the trailer.» Boshqa feʼllardan keyin «to» + feʼlning asosiy shakli keladi (infinitiv): want, need, plan, decide, agree. «She wants to become an owner-operator.»

Qaysi feʼldan keyin qaysi shakl kelishini aytadigan qisqa qoida yoʻq — har bir feʼlni yangi soʻz kabi alohida yodlash kerak. Haqiqiy haydovchilar suhbatining koʻp qismi uchun eng tez-tez uchraydigan feʼllarning qisqa roʻyxati yetarli.
ru: После некоторых глаголов идёт другой глагол с окончанием -ing (герундий): enjoy, avoid, finish, practice, keep on. «I enjoy driving at night.» «We finished loading the trailer.» После других глаголов идёт «to» + начальная форма (инфинитив): want, need, plan, decide, agree. «She wants to become an owner-operator.»

Короткого правила, какой глагол за какой формой следует, нет — каждый глагол нужно выучить отдельно, как новое слово. Для большинства реальных разговоров дальнобойщиков хватает короткого списка самых частых глаголов.

examples.en: I enjoy driving long routes.
examples.ru: Мне нравится ездить по длинным маршрутам.

examples.en: She wants to become an owner-operator.
We finished loading the trailer.
He avoided hitting the pothole.
They plan to leave at 5 AM.
examples.uz: Ular ertalab soat 5 da joʻnashni rejalashtirmoqda.

mistake.wrong: I want driving fast. She enjoys to drive at night.
mistake.right: I want to drive fast. She enjoys driving at night.

why.en: Uzbek doesn't have this to/-ing split, so after a verb like 'want' (xohlamoq) it feels natural to just add -ing the same way you would after 'enjoy.' Which pattern a verb takes has to be memorized case by case.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida bu to/-ing boʻlinishi yoʻq, shuning uchun 'want' (xohlamoq) kabi feʼldan keyin ham 'enjoy' dan keyingidek -ing qoʻshish tabiiy tuyuladi. Qaysi qolip kerakligini har bir feʼl uchun alohida yodlash kerak.
why.ru: В узбекском нет такого деления на to/-ing, поэтому после глагола вроде 'want' (xohlamoq) кажется естественным просто добавить -ing, как после 'enjoy'. В русском после «хочу» и «люблю» тоже идёт просто инфинитив, так что легко перепутать. Какая форма нужна, приходится запоминать для каждого глагола отдельно.

teach: Give students a short list of 'gerund verbs' (enjoy, avoid, finish, practice) vs 'infinitive verbs' (want, need, plan, decide) and have them memorize it like vocabulary, not a grammar rule — there's no shortcut, so treat each verb as its own flashcard.
Quick drill: say a verb from the list and have each driver make one true sentence about their own job on the spot — this builds the habit faster than worksheets.

title.uz: Majhul nisbat — sodir boʻlgan voqeani bildirish
title.ru: Страдательный залог — сообщаем, что произошло

rule.uz: Majhul nisbat 'was/were' yoki 'is/are' + feʼlning III shakli bilan yasaladi va harakatni kim qilgani emas, nima sodir boʻlganiga urgʻu beradi.
rule.ru: Страдательный залог образуется с was/were или is/are + третья форма глагола и подчёркивает, что произошло, а не кто это сделал.

en: Use the passive voice (was/were, or is/are + the past participle) when the action matters more than who did it — this is common in reports: "The trailer was loaded at 6 AM" focuses on what happened, not who loaded it.
Form it with is/are (present) or was/were (past) + the past participle of the verb: "The truck is inspected every morning." "The load was delivered on time."
uz: Majhul nisbat (was/were yoki is/are + oʻtgan zamon sifatdoshi) harakatning oʻzi uni kim bajarganidan muhimroq boʻlganda ishlatiladi — bu hisobotlarda odatiy: «The trailer was loaded at 6 AM» kim yuklaganini emas, nima boʻlganini aytadi.
U is/are (hozirgi zamon) yoki was/were (oʻtgan zamon) + feʼlning III shakli bilan yasaladi: «The truck is inspected every morning.» «The load was delivered on time.»
ru: Страдательный залог (was/were или is/are + причастие прошедшего времени) используют, когда важно само действие, а не тот, кто его совершил — это типично для отчётов: «The trailer was loaded at 6 AM» говорит о том, что произошло, а не о том, кто грузил.
Он образуется с is/are (настоящее) или was/were (прошедшее) + третья форма глагола: «The truck is inspected every morning.» «The load was delivered on time.»

examples.en: The truck was inspected this morning.
The load was delivered on time.
The brakes were checked before the trip.
The paperwork is signed at the dock.
The accident was reported to dispatch.

mistake.wrong: The truck inspected this morning. The load delivered yesterday.
mistake.right: The truck was inspected this morning. The load was delivered yesterday.

why.en: Uzbek passive forms (masalan, 'tekshirildi') are a single word, so it's easy to forget the English 'was/were' helper and use only the past participle — English always needs the be-verb.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida majhul nisbat bitta soʻz ('tekshirildi'), shuning uchun inglizcha was/were yordamchi feʼlini unutib, faqat sifatdoshni qoldirish oson. Inglizchada bu bogʻlovchi feʼl doim kerak.
why.ru: В узбекском (как и в русском) страдательная форма — одно слово («tekshirildi» — «был проверен»), поэтому легко забыть английский вспомогательный глагол was/were и оставить одно причастие. В английском глагол-связка нужен всегда.

opts: The truck was fixed by the mechanic.
The mechanic is fixing the truck.

q.en: The report ___ (send) to dispatch this morning.
q.uz: Toʻldiring: 'The report ___ (send) to dispatch this morning.'
q.ru: Дополните: 'The report ___ (send) to dispatch this morning.'

q.uz: Toʻldiring: 'All drivers ___ (require) to log their hours.'

teach: Passive voice is genuinely useful for real DOT/incident reports, where a driver needs to describe what happened without pointing blame ('the trailer was damaged' rather than 'I damaged the trailer') — frame it that way rather than as an abstract rule.
Drill: give a short incident scenario (e.g. a flat tire) and have the driver describe it in 2-3 passive sentences, like a real report.

title.en: Tag Questions — aren't you? / didn't you?
title.uz: Qoʻshimcha savollar — arenʼt you? / didnʼt you?
title.ru: Разделительные вопросы — aren't you? / didn't you?

rule.uz: Gap tasdiq boʻlsa, oxiridagi qisqa savol inkor boʻladi; gap inkor boʻlsa, qisqa savol tasdiq boʻladi.
rule.ru: Если высказывание утвердительное, короткий вопрос в конце отрицательный; если высказывание отрицательное — вопрос утвердительный.

en: A tag question is a short question added to the end of a statement, used to confirm something or start small talk: "You're new here, aren't you?" If the sentence is positive, the tag is negative (aren't you); if the sentence is negative, the tag is positive (did you).
The tag matches the main verb: "You are... aren't you?" "You can... can't you?" "You didn't... did you?" Truckers use these constantly in casual talk with dispatchers and other drivers.
uz: Qoʻshimcha savol — gap oxiriga qoʻshiladigan qisqa savol; u aytilgan fikrni tasdiqlash yoki oddiy suhbatni boshlash uchun ishlatiladi: «Youʼre new here, arenʼt you?» Gap tasdiq boʻlsa, qoʻshimcha savol inkor boʻladi (arenʼt you); gap inkor boʻlsa, qoʻshimcha savol tasdiq boʻladi (did you).

Qoʻshimcha savol asosiy feʼlga mos keladi: «You are... arenʼt you?» «You can... canʼt you?» «You didnʼt... did you?» Haydovchilar dispetcherlar va boshqa haydovchilar bilan oddiy suhbatda bunday savollarni doim ishlatishadi.
ru: Разделительный вопрос — это короткий вопрос в конце утверждения, которым подтверждают сказанное или начинают непринуждённый разговор: «You're new here, aren't you?» («Вы здесь новенький, не так ли?»). Если предложение утвердительное, «хвостик» отрицательный (aren't you); если предложение отрицательное, «хвостик» утвердительный (did you).

«Хвостик» повторяет основной глагол: «You are... aren't you?» «You can... can't you?» «You didn't... did you?» Дальнобойщики постоянно используют такие вопросы в разговорах с диспетчерами и другими водителями.

examples.en: You're the new driver, aren't you?
examples.ru: Вы новый водитель, не так ли?

examples.en: You didn't forget the paperwork, did you?
This is your first route, isn't it?
examples.uz: Bu sizning birinchi marshrutingiz, shunday emasmi?
examples.ru: Это ваш первый рейс, не так ли?

examples.en: You can drive a manual, can't you?
examples.uz: Siz mexanika bilan hayday olasiz, shunday emasmi?
examples.ru: Вы умеете водить машину с механикой, не так ли?

examples.en: The load isn't ready yet, is it?

mistake.wrong: You are new here, are you? He can drive, can he?
mistake.right: You are new here, aren't you? He can drive, can't he?

why.en: Since Uzbek has no positive/negative flip like this, it feels natural to just repeat the same verb form — but English tags almost always flip polarity: a positive statement gets a negative tag, and the reverse.
why.uz: Oʻzbek tilida bunday tasdiq/inkor almashinuvi yoʻq, shuning uchun feʼlning xuddi shu shaklini takrorlash tabiiy tuyuladi — inglizchada esa qoʻshimcha savol deyarli har doim qutbni almashtiradi: tasdiq gapga inkor savol, inkor gapga tasdiq savol qoʻshiladi.
why.ru: В узбекском нет такой смены утверждения на отрицание (в русском есть неизменное «не так ли?»), поэтому кажется естественным просто повторить ту же форму глагола — но в английском «хвостик» почти всегда меняет полярность: утверждение получает отрицательный хвост, и наоборот.

teach: Tag questions are almost entirely about the flip in polarity (positive statement to negative tag, or the reverse) — drill this pattern out loud rather than explaining the grammar term; most students pick it up faster by ear than by rule.
Quick pair drill: one driver makes a true statement about the other ('You're from Tashkent'), the partner adds the correct tag out loud ('...aren't you?') and confirms or corrects it.

title.en: Confusing Word Pairs — too / either, a little / a few, still / yet
title.uz: Chalkashtiriladigan soʻz juftliklari — too / either, a little / a few, still / yet
title.ru: Путаемые пары слов — too / either, a little / a few, still / yet

rule.uz: Bu soʻz juftliklari oʻzbek tilidagi bitta soʻzga toʻgʻri kelmaydi, shuning uchun gap turi (tasdiq/inkor, sanaladigan/sanalmaydigan)ga qarab toʻgʻri soʻzni tanlash kerak.
rule.ru: Эти пары слов не соответствуют одному слову в узбекском (и русском), поэтому нужное слово выбирают по типу предложения (утверждение/отрицание, исчисляемое/неисчисляемое).

en: 'Too' agrees with a positive statement ("I'm tired too"); 'either' agrees with a negative one ("I'm not tired either"). 'A little' is for uncountable nouns (a little fuel), 'a few' is for countable ones (a few miles).

'Still' means something is continuing ("I'm still driving"); 'yet' is used in questions or negatives about something expected ("Are we there yet?" "I haven't arrived yet"). 'Lend' means giving something (I'll lend you my wrench); 'borrow' means receiving it (Can I borrow your wrench?).
uz: 'Too' tasdiq gapga mos keladi («Iʼm tired too»), 'either' esa inkor gapga («Iʼm not tired either»). 'A little' sanalmaydigan otlar uchun (a little fuel), 'a few' esa sanaladigan otlar uchun (a few miles).

'Still' biror narsa davom etayotganini bildiradi («Iʼm still driving»); 'yet' esa kutilgan narsa haqidagi savol va inkorlarda ishlatiladi («Are we there yet?» «I havenʼt arrived yet»). 'Lend' — biror narsani bermoq (Iʼll lend you my wrench); 'borrow' — olmoq (Can I borrow your wrench?).
ru: 'Too' используется в утверждении («I'm tired too» — «Я тоже устал»), а 'either' — в отрицании («I'm not tired either» — «Я тоже не устал»). 'A little' — для неисчисляемых существительных (a little fuel — немного топлива), 'a few' — для исчисляемых (a few miles — несколько миль).

'Still' означает, что что-то продолжается («I'm still driving» — «Я всё ещё за рулём»); 'yet' используется в вопросах и отрицаниях об ожидаемом («Are we there yet?» — «Мы уже приехали?», «I haven't arrived yet» — «Я ещё не приехал»). 'Lend' — давать что-то («I'll lend you my wrench» — «Я одолжу тебе свой ключ»); 'borrow' — брать («Can I borrow your wrench?» — «Можно взять твой ключ?»).

examples.en: I'm hungry too. — I'm not hungry either.
examples.uz: Men ham ochman. — Men ham och emasman.
examples.ru: Я тоже голоден. — Я тоже не голоден.

examples.en: We have a little fuel left.
We have a few miles left.
We haven't arrived yet.
Can I borrow your flashlight? — Sure, I'll lend it to you.
examples.ru: Можно взять ваш фонарик? — Конечно, я вам его одолжу.

mistake.wrong: I'm not tired too. We have a little miles left.
mistake.right: I'm not tired either. We have a few miles left.

why.en: These pairs don't map onto single Uzbek words, so it's easy to use the same word (e.g. 'ham' for both too/either) in both positive and negative sentences, or to mix up countable and uncountable nouns.
why.uz: Bu juftliklar oʻzbek tilidagi bitta soʻzga toʻgʻri kelmaydi, shuning uchun bitta soʻzni (masalan, 'ham') ham tasdiq, ham inkor gaplarda ishlatish yoki sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlarni aralashtirish oson.
why.ru: Эти пары не сводятся к одному слову в узбекском (и русском «тоже»), поэтому легко использовать одно и то же слово (например, «ham»/«тоже») и в утверждениях, и в отрицаниях, или путать исчисляемые и неисчисляемые существительные.

q.ru: Дополните: 'He didn't sleep well, and I didn't ___.'

teach: These pairs don't translate cleanly to Uzbek, so drilling them as fixed chunks (I'm tired too / I'm not tired either) works better than explaining the rule abstractly — have students repeat both versions of each pair back to back.
Borrow/lend is worth a quick role-play: one driver asks to borrow a tool, the other offers to lend it — this is a genuinely common real exchange at a truck stop.

title.uz: Haydovchilar ishlatadigan feʼl+old koʻmakchi birikmalar — II
title.ru: Фразовые глаголы, которые используют дальнобойщики — II

rule.uz: Bu feʼl birikmalarining maʼnosi ham soʻzma-soʻz tarjimadan chiqmaydi — har birini alohida soʻz sifatida yodlash kerak.
rule.ru: Значение этих сочетаний глагола с частицей тоже не выводится из дословного перевода — каждое нужно запоминать как отдельное слово.

en: More phrasal verbs common on the road: back up (reverse), pull out (leave a spot), turn off (shut down the engine), run out of (have none left), watch out for (be alert to a hazard), hold up (delay), catch up (get caught up on something behind).

Some of these need a preposition after them to complete the meaning — run out OF fuel, watch out FOR ice. Dropping that small word changes or breaks the meaning, so learn the whole phrase together, preposition included.
uz: Yoʻlda tez-tez uchraydigan yana frazal feʼllar: back up (orqaga yurmoq), pull out (joydan chiqmoq), turn off (dvigatelni oʻchirmoq), run out of (biror narsa tugab qolmoq), watch out for (xavfdan ehtiyot boʻlmoq), hold up (kechiktirmoq), catch up (orqada qolganini yetib olmoq).

Ularning baʼzilariga maʼnoni toʻldirish uchun yana predlog kerak — run out OF fuel, watch out FOR ice. Bu kichik soʻzni tushirib qoldirish maʼnoni oʻzgartiradi yoki buzadi, shuning uchun iborani predlog bilan birga butunicha yodlang.
ru: Ещё фразовые глаголы, частые в дороге: back up (сдавать назад), pull out (выезжать с места), turn off (глушить двигатель), run out of (у кого-то что-то закончилось), watch out for (остерегаться опасности), hold up (задерживать), catch up (нагонять, догонять отставшее).

Некоторым из них после частицы нужен ещё предлог для завершения смысла — run out OF fuel, watch out FOR ice. Если опустить это маленькое слово, смысл меняется или ломается, поэтому учите фразу целиком, вместе с предлогом.

examples.en: Back up slowly — I'll guide you.
examples.uz: Sekin orqaga yuring — men sizga yoʻl koʻrsataman.
examples.ru: Сдавайте назад медленно — я буду вас направлять.

examples.en: We pulled out of the yard at 5 AM.
examples.uz: Biz ertalab soat 5 da hovlidan chiqdik.
examples.ru: Мы выехали со двора в 5 утра.

examples.en: Turn off the engine before you check the oil.
examples.ru: Заглушите двигатель, прежде чем проверять масло.

examples.en: Don't run out of fuel on the highway.
examples.ru: Не оставайтесь без топлива на трассе.

examples.en: Watch out for black ice this morning.

mistake.wrong: I ran out gas. Watch out ice.
mistake.right: I ran out of gas. Watch out for ice.

why.en: Some phrasal verbs need a small connecting word (of, for) that's easy to drop since Uzbek doesn't mark it the same way — these three-word combinations are their own trap on top of the simpler two-word phrasal verbs.
why.uz: Baʼzi frazal feʼllarga (of, for) kabi kichik bogʻlovchi soʻz kerak, oʻzbek tilida u boshqacha ifodalangani uchun uni tushirib qoldirish oson — bu uch soʻzli birikmalar oddiy ikki soʻzli frazal feʼllardan ham oʻziga xos tuzoq.
why.ru: Некоторым фразовым глаголам нужно маленькое связующее слово (of, for), которое легко пропустить, потому что в узбекском (и русском) оно выражается иначе — эти трёхсловные сочетания — отдельная ловушка поверх более простых двухсловных фразовых глаголов.

q.ru: Какой фразовый глагол требует 'of' сразу после себя?

teach: Phrasal verbs are pure memorization — there's no shortcut rule, so treat each one exactly like a vocabulary flashcard rather than trying to explain the grammar behind it.
Good classroom drill: act out or mime the phrasal verb (backing up, turning a key to turn off) while saying the sentence — physical action plus the phrase sticks better than the phrase alone.
